detector:alice.name: ALICE detector

specs.calorimeters: Two electromagnetic calorimeters, PHOS and EMCal
specs.muon_system: Forward muon arm (2-9 degrees polar angle): absorbers, a large dipole magnet, and fourteen planes of tracking and triggering chambers
specs.pseudorapidity_coverage: Central barrel |eta| < 0.9 (TPC/TOF; TRD |eta| < 0.84); forward muon spectrometer 2.5 < |eta| < 4.0 (polar angle 2-9 degrees)
specs.tracker: Inner Tracking System (six planes: silicon pixel/SPD, drift/SDD, strip/SSD) plus a cylindrical Time-Projection Chamber (TPC); the TRD also contributes to tracking

subsystems: Inner Tracking System (ITS): six planes of silicon pixel (SPD), drift (SDD) and strip (SSD) detectors
Time-Projection Chamber (TPC): main tracking and dE/dx particle-identification detector
Time-of-Flight (TOF), Ring Imaging Cherenkov (HMPID) and Transition Radiation (TRD) arrays for particle identification
Forward muon spectrometer: absorbers, dipole magnet, and fourteen tracking/triggering chamber planes

summary.plain: A 10,000-tonne detector at CERN built to study collisions of lead nuclei. Layers of tracking and identification detectors sit inside a large recycled magnet, surrounded by a forward arm that catches muons, letting physicists reconstruct the thousands of particles each collision produces.

detector:alice.technology: Central barrel of silicon/gas tracking, PID and calorimetry detectors inside a solenoid magnet, plus a forward muon spectrometer

detector:alps-ii.name: ALPS II apparatus

summary.plain: ALPS II shines a laser at a wall to see if a tiny fraction of the light can sneak through as an undetectable particle and turn back into light on the far side, which would be a sign of new, very light particles.

detector:alps-ii.technology: Light-shining-through-a-wall apparatus: a laser beam is enhanced in a build-up optical cavity, blocked by a light-tight wall, with a second, identical regeneration cavity and superconducting dipole magnets (reused HERA magnets) on both sides, and a low-noise single-photon/heterodyne detector looking for regenerated photons on the far side.

detector:anita.name: ANITA payload

summary.plain: A ring of radio antennas hanging beneath a giant NASA balloon, floating 37 kilometres over Antarctica and listening for the radio crackle of a neutrino hitting the ice far below.

detector:anita.technology: Balloon-borne array of quad-ridged horn antennas detecting radio-frequency Askaryan-effect pulses from neutrino- and cosmic-ray-induced showers in Antarctic ice

detector:antares.name: ANTARES detector

summary.plain: Twelve long cables strung with light-sensing glass spheres, anchored to the Mediterranean seabed off Toulon, France. Together they watched a huge volume of seawater for the faint blue light that a neutrino leaves behind.

detector:antares.technology: Deep-sea water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: photomultiplier tubes in pressure-resistant glass spheres (optical modules) on vertical mooring lines

detector:ara.name: ARA stations

summary.plain: Five separate stations of radio antennas buried in the ice near the South Pole, each listening on its own for the radio flash of an ultra-high-energy neutrino.

detector:ara.technology: Autonomous in-ice radio (Askaryan-effect) detector stations, each an independent array of radio antennas buried 100-200 m deep in the ice

detector:arianna.name: ARIANNA Hexagonal Radio Array

summary.plain: A small hexagon of radio-antenna stations that once sat on the surface of the Ross Ice Shelf, each one a self-contained listening post for neutrino signals.

detector:arianna.technology: Surface-deployed radio antenna stations detecting Askaryan-effect radio pulses from neutrino interactions in the ice below

detector:atlas.name: ATLAS detector

specs.calorimeters: Liquid-argon electromagnetic calorimeter with accordion geometry kept at -184 C, scintillator-tile hadronic calorimeter of about 420 000 tiles weighing almost 2900 tonnes, and liquid-argon hadronic end-cap and forward calorimeters
specs.muon_system: Air-core toroid muon spectrometer with three layers of precision tracking chambers - monitored drift tubes, plus resistive plate, thin-gap, small-strip thin-gap chambers and Micromegas for triggering
specs.pseudorapidity_coverage: Precision tracking |eta| < 2.5; electromagnetic calorimetry |eta| < 3.2 extended to |eta| = 4.9 by the forward calorimeters; muon spectrometer |eta| < 2.7 (trigger 2.4)
specs.tracker: Silicon pixel detector (92 million pixels, innermost layer 3.3 cm from the beam), semiconductor tracker (about 4000 modules, 6 million silicon micro-strips over 60 m^2) and transition radiation tracker (300 000 thin-walled drift tubes)

subsystems.description: Pixel detector, semiconductor tracker and transition radiation tracker inside the 2 T solenoid, reconstructing charged-particle tracks and vertices for |eta| < 2.5
subsystems.name: Inner Detector

subsystems.description: Accordion-geometry lead/liquid-argon sampling calorimeter measuring electron and photon energies; barrel 6.4 m long, 53 cm thick, 110 000 channels, held at -184 C
subsystems.name: Liquid-argon electromagnetic calorimeter

subsystems.description: Steel and plastic-scintillator sampling calorimeter of about 420 000 tiles and 9500 photomultipliers weighing almost 2900 tonnes, measuring hadron and jet energies in the barrel region
subsystems.name: Tile hadronic calorimeter

subsystems.description: Three layers of precision chambers in the air-core toroid field, including 1171 monitored-drift-tube chambers with 354 240 tubes, and wheels 25 m in diameter at each end
subsystems.name: Muon spectrometer

subsystems.description: Central superconducting solenoid giving 2 T in 4.5 cm of material with 38 MJ stored energy, a 25.3 m long barrel toroid of eight coils with 1.08 GJ stored, and two end-cap toroids with 0.25 GJ each
subsystems.name: Magnet system

subsystems.description: Two-stage trigger selecting interesting collisions out of up to 1.7 billion per second and writing about 1000 events per second to storage, with the first-level decision taken in under 2.5 microseconds
subsystems.name: Trigger and data acquisition

summary.plain: A cylinder 46 metres long and 25 metres across weighing 7000 tonnes - the largest particle detector ever built. Layers of tracking chambers, calorimeters and muon chambers wrap around the point where the two proton beams meet, so that almost everything produced in a collision leaves a trace somewhere.

detector:atlas.technology: General-purpose 4-pi collider detector with a thin superconducting solenoid around the inner-detector cavity and three large superconducting air-core toroids around the calorimeters

detector:babar.name: BaBar detector

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC built around the collision point of the PEP-II accelerator, layered so that it can pinpoint exactly where a B meson decayed and identify the particles it decayed into.

detector:babar.technology: Multi-layer silicon vertex tracker, cylindrical drift chamber, DIRC Cherenkov particle-ID detector, CsI electromagnetic calorimeter and resistive-plate-chamber muon system

detector:baikal-gvd.name: Baikal-GVD detector

summary.plain: Clusters of light-sensing spheres hanging on strings deep in Lake Baikal, added year after year since 2016, that together form a growing telescope for neutrinos from space.

detector:baikal-gvd.technology: Underwater water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: photomultiplier-equipped optical modules on vertical strings organised into clusters

detector:belle.name: Belle detector

summary.plain: The large barrel-shaped particle detector that surrounded the collision point of the KEKB machine from 1999 to 2010. A powerful magnet bent the tracks of the particles produced so that their momenta could be measured.

detector:belle.technology: general-purpose 4π magnetic spectrometer built around a 1.5 T superconducting solenoid

detector:belle-ii.name: Belle II detector

subsystems.description: Two layers of pixelated silicon sensors immediately around the beam pipe, measuring decay-vertex positions. A new, fully implemented pixel detector was installed during Long Shutdown 1.
subsystems.name: PXD — pixel vertex detector

subsystems.description: Four layers of double-sided silicon strip sensors surrounding the PXD.
subsystems.name: SVD — silicon vertex detector

subsystems.description: The main tracking device: a large gas volume strung with sense and field wires that measures charged-particle trajectories, momenta and specific ionisation (dE/dx).
subsystems.name: CDC — central drift chamber

subsystems.description: A barrel-shaped array of quartz-radiator Cherenkov counters used for charged-hadron identification.
subsystems.name: TOP — time-of-propagation counters

subsystems.description: A ring-imaging Cherenkov counter with an aerogel radiator in the forward end-cap, complementing the TOP for particle identification.
subsystems.name: ARICH — aerogel ring-imaging Cherenkov counter

subsystems.description: Scintillator crystals inside the solenoid that measure the energies of photons and electrons.
subsystems.name: ECL — electromagnetic calorimeter

subsystems.description: The instrumented iron flux return outside the solenoid, which detects long-lived neutral kaons and identifies muons.
subsystems.name: KLM — K-long and muon detector

summary.plain: The detector that records what comes out of the SuperKEKB collisions. Seven layers of instruments, wrapped in a strong magnet, track and identify the particles produced when electrons and positrons annihilate.

detector:belle-ii.technology: general-purpose 4π magnetic spectrometer with seven subdetectors inside a 1.5 T superconducting solenoid

detector:borexino.name: Borexino detector

summary.plain: A nylon sphere full of ultra-pure liquid, watched by photomultiplier tubes, that catches the faint flashes of light neutrinos leave behind as they pass through.

detector:borexino.technology: A nylon-sphere vessel of pseudocumene+PPO liquid scintillator viewed by photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by buffer liquid and a water-Cherenkov muon veto

detector:cast.name: CAST detector

summary.plain: The CAST detector reused a retired magnet originally built for the Large Hadron Collider, pointed it at the Sun, and looked for the faint X-rays that would appear if hypothetical axion particles convert into light inside the magnet.

detector:cast.technology: Axion helioscope: a decommissioned LHC prototype superconducting dipole magnet, pointed at the Sun, with its hollow beam-pipe bores acting as viewing tubes for X-ray optics and X-ray detectors that look for photons produced by solar axions converting in the magnetic field.

detector:cdf.name: CDF detector

specs.calorimeters: 23 layers of lead and scintillating plastic (electromagnetic) and 23 layers of steel and scintillating plastic (hadronic) sampling calorimeters
specs.muon_system: Outer layer of muon drift chambers catching muons that pass through the calorimeters
specs.tracker: 7 layers of silicon microstrip detectors around the beam pipe plus a large open-cell drift ("wire") chamber recording up to 96 position measurements per particle

summary.plain: A four-story-tall, roughly 4,500-tonne particle detector built around the point where Fermilab's Tevatron collided protons with antiprotons, used to trace and measure the particles produced.

detector:cdf.technology: General-purpose solenoidal collider detector with silicon and drift-chamber tracking, sampling calorimetry and muon chambers

detector:cdms-ii.name: CDMS II detector

description: Five towers, each containing six detectors (disks ~10 mm thick, 76 mm in diameter)
subsystems.name: Towers

summary.plain: Thirty disk-shaped crystals of germanium and silicon, each about the size of a hockey puck, cooled to below one-twentieth of a degree above absolute zero to catch the faint recoil of a dark matter particle hitting an atom.

detector:cdms-ii.technology: Cryogenic germanium and silicon detectors reading both ionization and phonon (heat) signals from particle recoils, arranged in towers

detector:cms.name: CMS detector

specs.calorimeters: lead-tungstate (PbWO4) scintillating-crystal electromagnetic calorimeter and brass-scintillator sampling hadron calorimeter, with forward sampling calorimeters
specs.muon_system: four stations of muon detectors instrumenting the iron flux-return yoke: drift tubes and resistive plate chambers in the barrel, cathode strip chambers, resistive plate chambers and GEM chambers in the endcaps

subsystems.description: The largest superconducting magnet ever built; its coils and iron return yoke dominate the detector mass and the yoke is 14 m in diameter.
subsystems.name: Superconducting solenoid

subsystems.description: All-silicon pixel and strip tracker covering an area the size of a tennis court with 135 million readout channels and ~10 µm single-point accuracy.
subsystems.name: Silicon tracker

subsystems.description: Lead-tungstate (PbWO4) scintillating crystals that stop electrons and photons and measure their energy.
subsystems.name: Electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL)

subsystems.description: Brass and scintillator sampling calorimeter that stops hadrons passing through the ECAL.
subsystems.name: Hadron calorimeter (HCAL)

subsystems.description: 1400 muon chambers embedded in the steel return yoke: drift tubes, cathode strip chambers, resistive plate chambers and GEM chambers.
subsystems.name: Muon system

subsystems.description: A two-level trigger reduces the 40 MHz bunch-crossing rate to about 100 kHz at Level-1 and to about 100 events per second after the High-Level Trigger.
subsystems.name: Trigger and data acquisition

summary.plain: A 21-metre-long, 14 000-tonne particle detector wrapped around one of the points where the Large Hadron Collider's proton beams cross. Its huge magnet bends the paths of the particles produced so that their momenta can be measured.

detector:cms.technology: general-purpose 4π collider detector built around a 3.8 T superconducting solenoid, with an all-silicon tracker, a lead-tungstate crystal electromagnetic calorimeter, a brass/scintillator sampling hadron calorimeter and muon detectors in the iron flux-return yoke

summary.plain: A 22-kilogram tank of liquid argon that made the first measurement of coherent neutrino scattering off argon nuclei, a step toward the argon detectors used by much larger neutrino and dark-matter experiments.
A 14.6-kilogram crystal of caesium iodide that made the first direct observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, a process predicted for decades but never before caught.

intervals.label: Ge-Mini operation, evidence of CEvNS on germanium

detector:coherent-ge.name: COHERENT germanium array (Ge-Mini)

summary.plain: An array of eight ultra-pure germanium crystals, together weighing about 17.6 kilograms, that in 2024 became the third type of atomic nucleus on which COHERENT caught neutrinos bouncing off gently.

detector:coherent-ge.technology: array of high-purity, p-type point-contact (inverted-coaxial) germanium spectrometers

summary.plain: A 185-kilogram array of sodium-iodide crystals used to measure background rates and study how neutrinos interact with iodine, a step toward a much larger planned sodium-iodide detector.

detector:comet.name: COMET detector

summary.plain: A curved tunnel of superconducting magnets at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan that bends and slows down muons, feeding them into a detector built to catch the single electron that would appear if a muon converted into one.

detector:comet.technology: Curved superconducting solenoid pion/muon transport (capture and transport solenoids) feeding a detector solenoid instrumented with cylindrical drift chamber and trigger hodoscope (CyDet, Phase-I) or straw tracker and electromagnetic calorimeter (StrECAL)

target_mass.display: 4 kg (4 x 1 kg) nominal; 2.83 +/- 0.02 kg active at Leibstadt

summary.plain: Four one-kilogram blocks of ultra-pure germanium, first used at a German nuclear plant and later moved to a Swiss one, sensitive enough to feel the tiny nudge of a reactor antineutrino bouncing off a whole atomic nucleus.

detector:cresst.name: CRESST cryogenic calorimeter array

specs.isotope: CaWO4 (CRESST-II/III main target); sapphire (Al2O3) in CRESST-I; lithium aluminate modules also deployed in CRESST-III

summary.plain: Small crystals, some no heavier than a coin, cooled colder than outer space and watched for the tiny flash of light and warmth made when a particle bumps an atom inside.

detector:cresst.technology: Cryogenic calorimeters with tungsten transition-edge sensors (TES) on scintillating crystal absorbers (sapphire in CRESST-I; CaWO4 from CRESST-II on), reading both a phonon (heat) and a scintillation-light channel

detector:ctao.name: CTAO telescope arrays

description: Four Large-Sized Telescopes planned in the northern array (La Palma) for the lowest energies, 20 GeV to 3 TeV.
subsystems.name: Large-Sized Telescopes (LST)

description: Up to 23 Medium-Sized Telescopes distributed over both array sites, covering 80 GeV to 50 TeV.
subsystems.name: Medium-Sized Telescopes (MST)

description: Up to 37 Small-Sized Telescopes planned in the southern array (Paranal) for the highest energies, above 2 TeV.
subsystems.name: Small-Sized Telescopes (SST)

summary.plain: Two big groups of gamma-ray telescopes, one in Spain and one in Chile, coming in three different sizes so together they can see the whole range of gamma-ray energies.

detector:ctao.technology: Two ground-based arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in three size classes (Large, Medium, Small).

summary.plain: 988 crystals of tellurium dioxide, cooled to a fraction of a degree above absolute zero, arranged in towers inside a giant refrigerator under an Italian mountain.
About 1500 crystals of lithium molybdate, designed to both flash light and register heat when a particle hits them, planned to fill CUORE's existing refrigerator under the Gran Sasso mountain.

detector:d0.name: D0 detector

specs.muon_system: Three outer layers of muon detectors surrounding the calorimeters
specs.tracker: Silicon detectors nested inside scintillating-fiber tracking detectors mounted on carbon-fiber supports (Run II)

summary.plain: A four-story-tall, roughly 5,500-tonne particle detector at Fermilab, named after its location on the Tevatron ring, built to trace and measure particles from proton-antiproton collisions with especially precise calorimeters.

detector:d0.technology: General-purpose collider detector with uranium/liquid-argon calorimetry, and (from Run II) silicon and fiber tracking inside a solenoidal magnet

detector:damic.name: DAMIC CCD array

summary.plain: A stack of camera-sensor-like silicon chips, cooled and shielded two kilometres underground at SNOLAB, watching for the faint trace of a dark matter particle bumping into a silicon atom.

detector:damic.technology: Thick, fully-depleted scientific CCDs for ionization detection, later supplemented with skipper-readout CCDs for single-electron sensitivity

detector:damic-m.name: DAMIC-M Low Background Chamber

summary.plain: A small, extremely quiet chamber of silicon chips deep under a mountain in France, sensitive enough to notice a single electron being knocked loose by a dark matter particle.

detector:damic-m.technology: Skipper-readout silicon CCDs providing single-electron ionization resolution

detector:darkside-20k.name: DarkSide-20k detector

summary.plain: A much larger tank of liquid argon than its predecessor DarkSide-50, holding fifty tonnes, being built deep under an Italian mountain to hunt for dark matter with thousands of tiny light sensors.

detector:darkside-20k.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid argon TPC with SiPM light readout

specs.shielding: 30 t organic liquid scintillator neutron veto inside a 1 kt water-Cherenkov muon veto

summary.plain: A small tank of liquid argon, about fifty kilograms of it, that watched for dark matter particles bumping into argon atoms deep under an Italian mountain.

detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.name: Daya Bay antineutrino detectors

target_mass.display: 20 t Gd-doped liquid scintillator per detector

summary.plain: A set of identical tank-like detectors, each holding 20 tonnes of a liquid that glows when antineutrinos interact in it, spread across near and far halls at Daya Bay.

detector:daya-bay-antineutrino-detectors.technology: Functionally identical cylindrical antineutrino detectors filled with gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator, viewed by photomultiplier tubes

detector:deap-3600.name: DEAP-3600 detector

specs.shielding: 2 km of rock overburden (6000 m.w.e.) at SNOLAB; no additional water or scintillator veto shield is described for DEAP-3600 in the sources fetched this session.

subsystems.description: A 5-cm-thick spherical acrylic vessel, 85 cm inner radius, holding up to 3600 kg of liquid argon (fiducial volume 1000 kg within 55 cm radius), viewed by 255 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-HQE PMTs that detect the 128 nm argon scintillation light after it is wavelength-shifted to the visible band by a tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coating.
subsystems.name: Acrylic vessel and PMT array

summary.plain: A sphere of 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon watched by 255 light sensors, 2 km underground in Canada. It looks for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make if it bumped into an argon atom, using only that light (no electric charge signal) to tell signal from background.

detector:deap-3600.technology: Single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector; unlike a two-phase argon or xenon TPC, DEAP-3600 has no drift field and no ionization/charge readout. It detects only scintillation light, collected by 255 PMTs, and uses the pulse shape of that scintillation signal (pulse-shape discrimination) to separate nuclear-recoil candidates from electromagnetic backgrounds.

detector:delphi.name: DELPHI detector

specs.tracker: Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) detectors for full charged-particle identification, plus a high-precision silicon vertex detector

subsystems.description: Differentiates between the various secondary charged particles using Cherenkov radiation rings.
subsystems.name: Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) system

subsystems.description: Advanced silicon tracking for precise detection of very short-lived particles.
subsystems.name: Silicon vertex detector

summary.plain: A roughly 10-metre cube of instruments at LEP's Point 8, famous for being able to tell exactly which kind of charged particle flew through it using rings of light (Cherenkov radiation).

detector:delphi.technology: General-purpose collider detector with Ring Imaging Cherenkov particle identification and precision silicon vertexing

detector:dmradio.name: DMRadio apparatus (DMRadio-m3 / DMRadio-50L)

summary.plain: DMRadio is a family of experiments being built at Stanford and SLAC that use a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit, instead of a microwave cavity, to search for very light dark-matter axions.

detector:dmradio.technology: Lumped-element resonant LC-circuit axion dark-matter search: a toroidal (DMRadio-50L) or solenoidal (DMRadio-m3) magnet coupled to a high-Q LC oscillator and SQUID readout, sensitive to sub-microwave-frequency axion-induced currents rather than a resonant cavity.

detector:donut.name: DONUT detector

summary.plain: A stack of nuclear-emulsion sheets and iron plates, backed by electronic trackers, that caught tau neutrinos as they interacted -- the first detector ever to do so directly.

detector:donut.technology: Nuclear-emulsion target with interspersed steel sheets, combined with electronic scintillator counters and drift chambers

detector:double-chooz.name: Double Chooz detectors

summary.plain: Two similar tank-shaped detectors of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator, one close to and one far from the Chooz reactors, catching antineutrino flashes of light.

detector:double-chooz.technology: Calorimetric liquid-scintillator detector consisting of four concentric cylindrical vessels, with a gadolinium-loaded liquid-scintillator target

detector:dune-far-detector-1.name: DUNE Far Detector Module 1 (horizontal drift)

cryostat_count.display: 1 cryostat, 15.1 m (w) x 14.0 m (h) x 62.0 m (l) internal

specs.readout: three module-length anode planes built from 150 anode plane assemblies (APAs), each 6 m high by 2.3 m wide, with three layers of active wires

total_mass.display: 17.5 kt of liquid argon per cryostat

subsystems.description: 150 wire-readout anode plane assemblies forming three 58.2 m long anode planes
subsystems.name: Anode plane assemblies (APAs)

subsystems.description: Four drift volumes at a 500 V/cm field, with a cathode high voltage of 180 kV
subsystems.name: Cathode planes and field cage

subsystems.description: Photon detectors supplementing the TPC and extending the physics reach
subsystems.name: Photon detection system

summary.plain: The first of four giant tanks of liquid argon nearly a mile underground in South Dakota. Charged particles from neutrino collisions leave trails of electrons that drift sideways onto walls of wires, producing a photograph-like picture of each event.

detector:dune-far-detector-1.technology: single-phase horizontal-drift liquid argon time projection chamber with anode plane assembly wire readout

detector:dune-far-detector-2.name: DUNE Far Detector Module 2 (vertical drift)

specs.readout: charge readout planes (CRPs) at the top and bottom of the two stacked drift volumes

summary.plain: The second DUNE far detector. It uses the same liquid argon idea as the first one, but the electrons drift up and down instead of sideways, which makes the detector simpler to build.

detector:dune-far-detector-2.technology: vertical-drift liquid argon time projection chamber with a horizontal cathode bisecting the detector and charge readout planes above and below

detector:dune-near-detector.name: DUNE Near Detector

specs.target_medium: liquid argon (ND-LAr), plus the SAND inner tracker targets

subsystems.description: Modular liquid argon TPC based on the ArgonCube design, the primary target and tracker of the near detector
subsystems.name: ND-LAr

subsystems.description: Day-1 muon spectrometer downstream of ND-LAr, to be replaced later by the gaseous argon detector ND-GAr
subsystems.name: TMS (Temporary Muon Spectrometer)

subsystems.description: Magnetised on-axis beam monitor with an inner tracker and electromagnetic calorimeter inside a large solenoid, reusing the KLOE magnet and calorimeter
subsystems.name: SAND

summary.plain: A set of smaller detectors on the Fermilab site, right where the neutrino beam is made. Measuring the beam before it travels lets scientists work out what changed by the time it reaches South Dakota.

detector:dune-near-detector.technology: composite near detector: a modular liquid argon TPC (ND-LAr), a muon spectrometer downstream of it, and a magnetised on-axis beam monitor (SAND)

detector:e949.name: E949 detector

summary.plain: The E949 detector stopped kaons inside itself and watched what happened next, looking for the rare case of a kaon turning into a pion and invisible particles.

detector:e949.technology: Stopped-kaon spectrometer: incoming kaons are brought to rest in an active target/scintillator stack, and the outgoing pion is tracked and its full decay chain (range, energy and kinematics) measured to reject backgrounds

detector:edelweiss.name: EDELWEISS germanium bolometer array

summary.plain: A block of ultra-pure germanium, cooled to near absolute zero deep under the French Alps, wired to catch both the tiny jolt of heat and the trickle of electric charge freed when a particle strikes an atom inside.

detector:edelweiss.technology: Cryogenic germanium bolometers reading both ionization (charge) and phonon (heat) signals; the current sub-GeV programme uses NbSi transition-edge sensors with Neganov-Trofimov-Luke phonon amplification

detector:exo-200.name: EXO-200 detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical tank of liquid xenon, chilled and shielded deep in a New Mexico salt mine, that watched for a rare radioactive decay by tracking both light and electric charge from each event.

detector:exo-200.technology: Liquid-xenon time projection chamber with combined charge/light readout

detector:faser.name: FASER detector

summary.plain: A compact particle detector in a disused CERN tunnel, combining a tracking spectrometer with a special emulsion-and-tungsten neutrino detector called FASERv.

detector:faser.technology: forward spectrometer with a tracking/magnet system and the FASERv emulsion-tungsten neutrino subdetector

detector:gallex-gno.name: GALLEX/GNO gallium target

summary.plain: A huge tank of gallium-laced liquid buried in an Italian mountain; when a low-energy solar neutrino hits a gallium atom, it turns into a germanium atom that scientists then count.

detector:gallex-gno.technology: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge, which is chemically extracted and counted; the target is a gallium trichloride-hydrochloric acid solution, not an electronic real-time detector

detector:gerda.name: GERDA detector

summary.plain: Bare germanium crystals submerged directly in a huge tank of ultra-cold liquid argon, deep under an Italian mountain, listening for a rare kind of radioactive decay.

detector:gerda.technology: Bare enriched-germanium point-contact detectors immersed in a liquid-argon cryostat

detector:grand.name: GRANDProto300 (GRAND prototype)

summary.plain: A prototype radio antenna array in the Gobi Desert in China, testing the technology for a much bigger planned array to detect cosmic rays and neutrinos.

detector:grand.technology: Surface radio antenna array detecting the radio pulses from extensive air showers and Earth-skimming neutrino-induced showers

detector:h-e-s-s.name: H.E.S.S. telescope array

description: Four 12 m diameter imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes arranged in a square, in operation since first light in 2002.
subsystems.name: Phase I telescopes (CT1-CT4)

description: A 28 m diameter telescope at the centre of the CT1-CT4 square, the largest Cherenkov telescope of its kind, lowering the array's energy threshold.
subsystems.name: CT5 (28 m telescope)

summary.plain: Five telescopes on a Namibian farm: four medium-sized ones in a square around one giant telescope, together watching for the blue flicker of light that gamma rays make hitting the atmosphere.

detector:h-e-s-s.technology: Hybrid array of four 12 m and one 28 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes.

detector:h1.name: H1 detector

summary.plain: A large, complex detector at DESY built around one of the two points on the HERA ring where electrons and protons collided, designed to catch and identify the particles produced.

detector:h1.technology: Complex general-purpose detector combining high-precision mechanical tracking, calorimetry and modern electronics/computing to detect particles from ep collisions

detector:hawc.name: HAWC water-Cherenkov array

summary.plain: An array of closed water tanks on a Mexican volcano that sense the faint flashes of light left by particles from gamma-ray and cosmic-ray showers as they pass through the water.

detector:hawc.technology: Array of closed water-Cherenkov detector tanks continuously sampling extensive air showers from gamma rays and cosmic rays.

detector:haystac.name: HAYSTAC detector

summary.plain: The HAYSTAC detector uses a strong magnet and a tunable metal cavity, plus quantum-noise-reducing electronics, to search for faint signals from dark-matter axions converting into radio photons.

detector:haystac.technology: Microwave-cavity haloscope using a strong static magnetic field (inverse Primakoff conversion) with quantum-electronics/cavity-QED readout, including a squeezed-vacuum receiver to beat the standard quantum noise limit.

detector:homestake.name: Homestake chlorine detector

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid, nearly a mile underground, that turned rare chlorine atoms into argon whenever a solar neutrino struck.

detector:homestake.technology: Radiochemical chlorine detector: solar neutrinos capture on 37Cl to produce 37Ar via inverse beta decay in a large tank of perchloroethylene (dry-cleaning fluid), with the argon periodically extracted and counted

detector:hyper-kamiokande.name: Hyper-Kamiokande detector

subsystems.description: New large-aperture, high-quantum-efficiency PMTs (up to 40,000 in the comparison-table maximum design; ~20,000 stated as the photosensor count elsewhere on the same site) viewing the main tank volume.
subsystems.name: Inner Detector

subsystems.description: Up to 10,000 smaller (8 cm-class) photosensors instrumenting the outer veto region.
subsystems.name: Outer Detector

subsystems.description: About 1,000 'compound eye' modules bundling multiple 8 cm PMTs for improved timing accuracy.
subsystems.name: Compound-eye photosensors

summary.plain: A huge new water tank being built underground near Kamioka: 68 metres across and 71 metres tall, more than five times the volume of Super-Kamiokande, ringed with tens of thousands of new light sensors.

detector:hyper-kamiokande.technology: Large cylindrical water Cherenkov tank, the successor design to Super-Kamiokande, instrumented with new high-sensitivity large-aperture PMTs and multi-PMT 'compound-eye' photosensor modules.

detector:iaxo.name: IAXO / BabyIAXO detector

summary.plain: The IAXO detector design uses a large magnet aimed at the Sun to catch faint signals from hypothetical axion particles. A smaller version, BabyIAXO, is being built at DESY as a stepping stone to the full-scale instrument.

detector:iaxo.technology: Axion helioscope: a purpose-built double-bore (IAXO) / toroidal (BabyIAXO) superconducting magnet tracking the Sun, coupled to X-ray focusing optics and low-background X-ray detectors, scaling up the CAST technique.

detector:icarus-t600.name: ICARUS T600

subsystems.description: cosmic ray tagger surrounding the cryostats, needed because the detector operates at shallow depth at Fermilab
subsystems.name: Cosmic Ray Tagger

summary.plain: A 760-tonne liquid argon detector, the first of its size ever built. It worked under an Italian mountain from 2010 to 2013, was rebuilt at CERN, and now sits at Fermilab as the far detector of a search for a possible fourth kind of neutrino.

detector:icarus-t600.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber in two adjacent modules

detector:icecube.name: IceCube in-ice array

specs.energy_range: Roughly 100 GeV to the PeV scale and above in the main array; about 10 GeV with the DeepCore infill

subsystems.description: Pressure sphere holding a ten-inch photomultiplier tube with on-board digitisation electronics
subsystems.name: Digital optical module (DOM)

subsystems.description: 86 strings on a hexagonal grid with 125 m horizontal spacing, 60 DOMs each, 17 m vertical separation
subsystems.name: String geometry

subsystems.description: Surface building that receives, digitises and time-stamps the DOM data
subsystems.name: IceCube Laboratory

summary.plain: The main part of IceCube: 86 cables lowered into holes melted in the ice, each carrying 60 basketball-sized light sensors that watch a cubic kilometre of ice for neutrino flashes.

detector:icecube.technology: In-ice Cherenkov array of digital optical modules frozen into the Antarctic ice sheet

detector:icecube-deepcore.name: DeepCore

specs.energy_range: Neutrino energy threshold lowered to about 10 GeV

subsystems.description: Horizontal separation about 70 m and vertical DOM spacing 7 m, versus 125 m and 17 m in the main array
subsystems.name: Dense string geometry

summary.plain: A tightly packed cluster of sensors in the middle of IceCube. Because the sensors sit closer together, it can see much fainter, lower-energy neutrinos, which is what makes IceCube able to study how neutrinos change type.

detector:icecube-deepcore.technology: Densely instrumented in-ice Cherenkov infill at the centre of the IceCube array

detector:icetop.name: IceTop

specs.energy_range: Air showers from primary cosmic rays in the 300 TeV to 1 EeV energy range

subsystems.description: Each of the 81 stations has two ice-filled tanks, each with two downward-facing DOMs
subsystems.name: Cherenkov tank pair

summary.plain: The part of IceCube that sits on the snow surface: 81 pairs of frozen water tanks that catch the showers of particles made when cosmic rays hit the atmosphere. It also helps IceCube tell cosmic rays apart from neutrinos.

detector:icetop.technology: Surface array of ice-filled Cherenkov tanks read out by downward-facing digital optical modules

detector:ingrid.name: INGRID (T2K on-axis near detector)

summary.plain: A cross-shaped array of iron-and-scintillator modules sitting directly in the path of T2K's neutrino beam, 280 metres from where the beam is made. It checks that the beam is pointed the right way and has the expected shape, run after run.

detector:ingrid.technology: On-axis array of iron/scintillator sandwich modules that measures the neutrino beam direction and profile.

intervals.label: detector support-structure, acrylic-vessel and PMT installation
filling with ultrapure water and liquid scintillator

detector:juno.name: JUNO central detector

description: A complementary array of 25,587 3-inch photomultiplier tubes providing an independent, non-saturating energy measurement alongside the 20-inch PMT array
subsystems.name: 3-inch PMT double-calorimeter array

description: A water-Cherenkov detector plus an overhead Top Tracker system used for muon detection and cosmogenic-background rejection
subsystems.name: Water Cherenkov veto and Top Tracker

summary.plain: A 20,000-tonne sphere of clear liquid, watched by more than 17,000 large light sensors and over 25,000 smaller ones, sitting inside a pool of water that screens out stray particles.

detector:juno.technology: 20-kiloton liquid-scintillator sphere viewed by large- and small-diameter photomultiplier tubes, immersed in a water-Cherenkov veto pool with an overhead Top Tracker

detector:kamland.name: KamLAND detector

summary.plain: A giant balloon of clear liquid inside a mine in Japan, watched by nearly 1,900 light sensors, that catches antineutrinos from nuclear reactors across the country. A xenon-loaded inner balloon suspended at its centre (KamLAND-Zen) uses the same detector to search for a different rare process.

detector:kamland.technology: Liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector: an 18-m-diameter spherical balloon of liquid scintillator viewed by photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a mineral-oil buffer and an outer water-Cherenkov muon veto

detector:karmen.name: KARMEN detector

summary.plain: A rectangular tank holding 65 cubic metres of liquid scintillator, split into 512 separate cells and laced with gadolinium to catch neutrons, sitting 18 metres from the ISIS accelerator's beam stop.

detector:karmen.technology: Segmented liquid-scintillation calorimeter with gadolinium-loaded module walls for neutron capture

detector:katrin.name: KATRIN spectrometer

summary.plain: A huge tube-shaped spectrometer that sorts electrons by their energy, precisely measuring the fastest ones released when radioactive tritium gas decays, to work out how heavy the neutrino can be.

detector:katrin.technology: MAC-E filter electrostatic/magnetic spectrometer with a windowless gaseous tritium source

aliases: Astroparticle Research with Cosmics in the Abyss

intervals.label: 51 detection units operating (current, undated official statement)

detector:km3net-arca.name: KM3NeT/ARCA

instrumented_volume.display: ~1 km3 (design, two building blocks of 115 detection units each)

string_count.display: 230 detection units (design: two building blocks of 115 each)

summary.plain: The bigger of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built for spotting very high-energy neutrinos from deep space. It sits 3500 metres down on the seabed off Sicily and, when finished, will fill about a cubic kilometre of seawater with light sensors.

detector:km3net-arca.technology: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules, each housing photomultiplier tubes, anchored to the Mediterranean seabed

aliases: Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss
detector:km3net-orca.name: KM3NeT/ORCA

instrumented_volume.display: ~0.007 km3 (~7 Mt of seawater; design, one building block of 115 detection units)

summary.plain: The smaller, more tightly packed of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built to study neutrinos made in Earth's atmosphere and work out how the three kinds of neutrino are ordered by mass. It sits 2450 metres down on the seabed off Toulon, France.

detector:km3net-orca.technology: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules with closer sensor spacing than ARCA, optimised for lower-energy atmospheric neutrinos

detector:koto.name: KOTO detector

summary.plain: The KOTO detector is a hermetic calorimeter and veto system in Japan that watches for the tell-tale flash of a neutral kaon decaying into a neutral pion and invisible particles, with nothing else visible.

detector:koto.technology: Hermetic electromagnetic calorimeter and veto-counter system surrounding a neutral-kaon beamline, reconstructing KL -> pi0 (-> gamma gamma) decays while vetoing all other visible particles

detector:ktev.name: KTeV detector

summary.plain: The KTeV detector combined a calorimeter, tracking chambers and veto systems to catch neutral kaons decaying, at Fermilab in the 1990s.

detector:ktev.technology: Neutral-kaon spectrometer with electromagnetic (CsI) calorimetry, drift chambers, a transition radiation detector system and photon/particle veto systems, used to reconstruct KL decays to two pions/photons

detector:l3.name: L3 detector

specs.calorimeters: Bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter, plus a hadronic calorimeter
specs.tracker: Silicon strip microvertex detector and a time-expansion chamber

subsystems.description: Bismuth-germanate crystal calorimeter giving very high resolution for electrons and photons.
subsystems.name: BGO electromagnetic calorimeter

subsystems.description: A very large solenoid magnet, later reused as ALICE's central magnet at the same LEP/LHC point.
subsystems.name: Solenoid magnet

summary.plain: A detector at LEP's Point 2 built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision, using dense bismuth-germanate crystals and one of the largest magnets ever built for a particle detector.

detector:l3.technology: Collider detector optimised for high-resolution electron, muon and photon measurement, built around a bismuth-germanate calorimeter and a very large solenoid magnet

detector:legend-200.name: LEGEND-200 detector

summary.plain: Up to 200 kilograms of enriched germanium detectors immersed in liquid argon in the same Italian underground hall used by the earlier GERDA experiment, watching for a rare radioactive decay.

detector:legend-200.technology: Enriched high-purity germanium detectors immersed in a liquid-argon active shield

detector:lhaaso.name: LHAASO multi-component array

summary.plain: A set of different kinds of ground detectors on a Chinese mountain, working together to sense cosmic-ray and gamma-ray showers in several ways at once.

detector:lhaaso.technology: Multi-component extensive-air-shower detector combining different shower-sampling techniques (electron, muon and Cherenkov/fluorescence light) at one high-altitude site.

detector:lhcb.name: LHCb detector

summary.plain: The LHCb detector is a single forward-pointing spectrometer, 21 metres long, 5600 tonnes, sitting 100 metres underground at CERN. Instead of surrounding the collision point on all sides like ATLAS or CMS, it stacks its sub-detectors one behind another to catch particles thrown forward by the collision.

detector:lhcb.technology: single-arm forward spectrometer with a warm dipole magnet, vertex locator (VELO), two RICH detectors, tracking stations, calorimeters and a muon system

detector:lhcf.name: LHCf detector

summary.plain: Two small, 40-kilogram detectors placed 140 metres either side of the ATLAS collision point, catching particles thrown almost exactly along the beam direction.

detector:lhcf.technology: two compact imaging sampling calorimeters (tungsten plates, plastic scintillator, position-sensitive sensors)

detector:lsnd.name: LSND detector

summary.plain: A cylindrical tank about 8 metres long holding 167 tonnes of mineral-oil scintillator, watched by more than a thousand light sensors, 30 metres from where the Los Alamos accelerator's beam produced neutrinos.

detector:lsnd.technology: Mineral-oil liquid scintillator detecting both Cherenkov and scintillation light, viewed by photomultiplier tubes

detector:lz.name: LZ detector

specs.shielding: Liquid xenon skin veto, a gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator outer detector, and an 8 m x 6 m tank of 70,000 gallons of ultrapure water, under ~1480 m of rock.

subsystems.description: Dual-phase xenon TPC about 1.5 m in diameter and height with a 145.6 cm drift region, read out by 253 top and 241 bottom 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410 PMTs.
subsystems.name: Liquid xenon time projection chamber

subsystems.description: An instrumented layer of about 2 tonnes of liquid xenon outside the TPC field cage, read out by 131 1-inch and 2-inch PMTs, used to veto gamma rays that scatter in both volumes.
subsystems.name: Xenon skin veto

subsystems.description: Acrylic tanks of gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator surrounding the cryostat, viewed by 120 Hamamatsu R5912 8-inch PMTs, tagging neutrons by capture on gadolinium.
subsystems.name: Outer detector

subsystems.description: A tank 8 m in diameter and 6 m high holding 70,000 gallons of purified water, which contains the outer detector and cryostat and suppresses gamma rays and neutrons from the cavern rock.
subsystems.name: Water shield

summary.plain: A tank of seven tonnes of cold liquid xenon, watched by hundreds of light sensors, that records the tiny flash and spark made if a dark matter particle bumps into a xenon atom. Layers of xenon, scintillator and water around it screen out ordinary radiation.

detector:lz.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid xenon time projection chamber

detector:magic.name: MAGIC telescopes

summary.plain: Two 17-metre dish telescopes on a Spanish island mountaintop, working together to catch the flicker of blue light made by gamma rays hitting the atmosphere.

detector:magic.technology: Two 17 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes operated stereoscopically.

detector:majorana-demonstrator.name: Majorana Demonstrator detector

isotope_mass.display: 40.4 kg total (27.2 kg enriched to ~88% in 76Ge)

summary.plain: Two modular arrays of ultra-pure germanium crystal detectors, kept in vacuum cryostats almost a mile underground in South Dakota, listening for a rare radioactive decay.

detector:majorana-demonstrator.technology: Modular arrays of high-purity germanium point-contact detectors in vacuum cryostats

detector:meg.name: MEG detector

summary.plain: A detector combining a tank of liquid xenon (to catch a gamma ray) with a tracking chamber (to catch a positron) at the Paul Scherrer Institute, looking for both particles appearing together from a single muon decay.

detector:meg.technology: Liquid xenon calorimeter for the gamma ray, combined with a drift chamber and timing counter spectrometer for the positron, on the PSI DC muon beamline

detector:meg-ii.name: MEG II detector

summary.plain: The upgraded version of the MEG detector: a finer liquid-xenon calorimeter and new tracking and timing detectors, at the same Swiss laboratory, still taking data.

detector:meg-ii.technology: Upgraded liquid xenon calorimeter with finer granularity, a new single-volume cylindrical drift chamber, upgraded timing counter and a new radiative decay counter, on the same PSI DC muon beamline

detector:microboone.name: MicroBooNE detector

summary.plain: A 170-tonne tank of liquid argon on the Booster neutrino beam at Fermilab that photographs neutrino collisions in three dimensions with wires instead of film. It was built to check a puzzling excess of events seen by an earlier experiment.

detector:microboone.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber

detector:minerva.name: MINERvA detector

subsystems.description: planes of graphite, iron and lead interleaved between tracking planes upstream of the scintillator tracker
subsystems.name: Passive nuclear targets

summary.plain: A compact, finely sliced detector sitting just in front of the MINOS near detector at Fermilab. Layers of graphite, iron, lead and water let it compare how neutrinos bounce off different kinds of atomic nucleus.

detector:minerva.technology: finely segmented scintillator-strip tracker with electromagnetic and hadronic sampling calorimetry and passive nuclear targets

detector:miniboone.name: MiniBooNE detector

summary.plain: A 12-metre sphere holding 818 tonnes of clear mineral oil, watched by 1,520 light sensors, 541 metres from where Fermilab makes its Booster neutrino beam. Flashes of light reveal the particles a neutrino leaves behind.

detector:miniboone.technology: spherical mineral-oil Cherenkov and scintillation detector viewed by photomultiplier tubes

subsystems.description: 486 octagonal steel-scintillator planes arranged in two supermodules
subsystems.name: Octagonal planes

summary.plain: A 5,400-tonne stack of 486 eight-sided steel and plastic plates, magnetised so it could tell neutrinos from antineutrinos, sitting 705 metres underground in an old Minnesota iron mine 735 kilometres from the beam.

The 980-tonne little sister of the MINOS far detector, in a cavern 100 metres below Fermilab about a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is born. It recorded the beam before any neutrinos had changed type.

detector:moedal.name: MoEDAL detector

summary.plain: MoEDAL's detector is mostly passive: 125 stacks of special plastic sheets that record the tracks of heavily-charged particles, plus about a tonne of metal to trap and hold onto anything unusual.

detector:moedal.technology: passive Nuclear Track Detector (NTD) stacks plus paramagnetic trapping volumes and TimePix pixel monitors

detector:mu2e.name: Mu2e detector

summary.plain: A 25-metre chain of giant superconducting magnets at Fermilab, with a tracker and a fast crystal detector at the end, built to catch the single electron that would appear if a muon ever turned into one.

detector:mu2e.technology: A 25-metre chain of three superconducting solenoids (production, transport, detector) feeding a straw-tube tracker and a fast CsI crystal calorimeter, surrounded by a cosmic-ray veto

detector:mu3e.name: Mu3e detector

summary.plain: A very thin, high-speed silicon camera built from custom pixel chips, combined with fast timing detectors, being assembled at the Paul Scherrer Institute to catch three particles flying apart from a single muon.

detector:mu3e.technology: Ultra-thin silicon pixel tracker built from high-voltage monolithic active pixel sensors (HV-MAPS), combined with scintillating-fibre and scintillating-tile timing detectors

intervals.label: storage ring relocated from BNL and reassembled at Fermilab (MC-1)

detector:muon-g-2.name: Muon g-2 storage ring

summary.plain: A 14-metre ring of superconducting magnet, originally built at Brookhaven and moved to Fermilab, that holds spinning muons in a very uniform magnetic field while detectors around its rim watch them wobble.

detector:muon-g-2.technology: Superconducting superferric muon storage ring with 24 electromagnetic calorimeter stations and straw tracking detectors around its circumference

detector:na48.name: NA48 detector

summary.plain: The NA48 detector combined a magnetic spectrometer and a calorimeter to track and measure kaon decay particles in an underground hall at CERN, confirming that CP violation happens directly in kaon decay.

detector:na48.technology: Magnetic spectrometer (helium-filled tank with two drift chambers either side of a dipole magnet) plus liquid-krypton electromagnetic calorimeter, used to reconstruct KL/KS -> 2 pion decays

detector:na62.name: NA62 detector

description: Low-mass, high-intensity silicon-pixel beam spectrometer providing 4D (position + time) tracking of individual beam particles at flux up to 2.0 MHz/mm^2, with 65 ps time resolution on tracks
subsystems.name: GigaTracker

summary.plain: The NA62 detector is a long chain of instruments in an underground hall at CERN, built to spot a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos. A precise beam tracker, a ring-shaped light detector and a calorimeter work together to reject almost everything else.

detector:na62.technology: Decay-in-flight kaon spectrometer: beam-tracking (GigaTracker), ring-imaging Cherenkov (RICH) particle identification, liquid-krypton (LKr) electromagnetic calorimeter and photon/particle veto systems around a large vacuum vessel

detector:na64.name: NA64 detector

summary.plain: The NA64 detector tags and tracks incoming electrons, absorbs their energy in a calorimeter, and watches for cases where energy simply vanishes -- a possible sign of an invisible dark-sector particle.

detector:na64.technology: Active beam-dump / missing-energy spectrometer: incoming electron tagged and tracked, its energy deposited in an electromagnetic calorimeter, with hermetic veto systems to catch any visible secondary particles so that missing energy signals an invisible decay

intervals.label: ND280 upgrade installed (Super-FGD, two High-Angle TPCs, TOF)
operating with the upgraded near detector

detector:nd280.name: ND280 (T2K off-axis near detector)

subsystems.description: Tracking planes of scintillating bars alternating with water-target/brass or lead foil, at the upstream end of the magnet.
subsystems.name: PØD (Pi-Zero Detector)

subsystems.description: Three gaseous time projection chambers interleaved with two fine-grained scintillator-bar detectors (FGDs), used to reconstruct charged-current interactions.
subsystems.name: Tracker (TPCs and FGDs)

subsystems.description: Surrounds the P0D and the tracker to detect gamma rays escaping the inner detectors.
subsystems.name: ECal (Electromagnetic Calorimeter)

subsystems.description: Scintillator instrumenting the return yoke of the magnet, measuring the range of muons exiting through the sides.
subsystems.name: SMRD (Side Muon Range Detector)

summary.plain: A stack of detectors inside a recycled particle-physics magnet, sitting just 280 metres from where T2K's neutrino beam is made. It measures the beam before the neutrinos have had a chance to change type, so physicists know what they started with.

detector:nd280.technology: Magnetized off-axis tracking detector: a water/brass Pi-Zero Detector (P0D), three gaseous time projection chambers and two fine-grained scintillator detectors as the tracker, surrounded by an electromagnetic calorimeter, all inside the recycled UA1 dipole magnet instrumented as a side muon range detector (SMRD).

detector:news-g.name: NEWS-G spherical proportional counter

summary.plain: A hollow copper sphere filled with gas and a tiny sensor at its centre, sensitive enough to notice a single electron freed when a particle bumps a gas atom.

detector:news-g.technology: Spherical proportional counter (SPC): a large gas-filled copper sphere with a single small sensor electrode at the centre, sensitive to single ionization electrons

summary.plain: A proposed tank of five tonnes of liquid xenon, planned for a deep Canadian mine, designed to be much more sensitive than its predecessor EXO-200.

detector:next-100.name: NEXT-100

summary.plain: The full-size NEXT detector, holding 100 kilograms of pressurized xenon gas, commissioned in 2024 at the Canfranc underground laboratory in Spain.

detector:next-100.technology: High-pressure xenon gas time projection chamber with electroluminescence readout

detector:next-white.name: NEXT-White

summary.plain: A smaller demonstration version of the NEXT detector, using high-pressure xenon gas, that ran at the Canfranc underground laboratory before the full-size NEXT-100 detector was built.

detector:next-white.technology: High-pressure xenon gas time projection chamber with electroluminescence readout

detector:nova-far-detector.name: NOvA far detector

subsystems.description: 344,000 cells of extruded, highly reflective plastic PVC filled with liquid scintillator (both NOvA detectors together)
subsystems.name: PVC cell array

summary.plain: A 14,000-tonne block of plastic tubes filled with a liquid that flashes when particles pass through, sitting on the surface in northern Minnesota. It catches the few neutrinos that survive an 810-kilometre trip from Chicago.

detector:nova-far-detector.technology: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, read out by avalanche photodiodes

detector:nova-near-detector.name: NOvA near detector

summary.plain: A small copy of the NOvA far detector, about 300 tonnes, sitting underground at Fermilab a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is made. It measures the beam before the neutrinos have had time to change type.

detector:nova-near-detector.technology: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, functionally identical to the far detector

detector:nucleus-calorimeter-array.name: NUCLEUS cryogenic calorimeter array

summary.plain: A tiny, extraordinarily sensitive detector made of a few grams of crystal, cooled almost to absolute zero, designed to feel the faint nudge of a reactor antineutrino bouncing off a whole atomic nucleus at the lowest energies yet attempted.

detector:nucleus-calorimeter-array.technology: gram-scale CaWO4/Al2O3 cryogenic calorimeters with active background discrimination, operated at millikelvin temperatures

detector:opal.name: OPAL detector

specs.calorimeters: Calorimeters as a middle layer of the concentric detector
specs.muon_system: Muon detectors as the outermost layer of the concentric detector
specs.tracker: Tracking detectors nearest the beam pipe, part of the concentric 'onion' layout

subsystems.description: Tracking, calorimeter and muon-detector layers arranged concentrically around the beam pipe.
subsystems.name: Layered ('onion') structure

summary.plain: A roughly 12-metre cube built in layers like an onion, so that every kind of particle from a LEP collision was caught by the right layer: tracking near the beam, then calorimeters, then muon detectors on the outside.

detector:opal.technology: General-purpose collider detector with tracking, calorimeter and muon layers arranged concentrically around the beam pipe

detector:opera.name: OPERA detector

summary.plain: A wall of about 150,000 bricks, each a stack of photographic film and lead sheets, arranged with electronic trackers and magnets, deep under Italy's Gran Sasso mountain.

detector:opera.technology: Lead/nuclear-emulsion 'brick' target-tracker (emulsion cloud chamber) with electronic scintillator trackers and magnetic muon spectrometers

aliases: STRing for Absorption length in Water
detector:p-one.name: P-ONE pathfinder instruments (STRAW / STRAW-b / P-ONE-1)

summary.plain: Small test strings of light and water sensors lowered into the deep Pacific to check the water and prove the technology before the full P-ONE telescope is built.

detector:p-one.technology: Deep-sea water Cherenkov pathfinder mooring lines instrumenting optical background and water-property measurements ahead of the full P-ONE array

summary.plain: A tank of liquid xenon -- six tonnes in total, four tonnes of it the active target -- that records flashes of light from particles hitting xenon nuclei, deep under a mountain in China.

detector:phenix.name: PHENIX detector

summary.plain: A multi-armed particle detector at Brookhaven's RHIC collider that tracked and identified particles from nuclear collisions between 2000 and 2016.

detector:phenix.technology: Multi-arm spectrometer combining central-arm tracking/calorimetry at midrapidity with forward/backward muon-arm spectrometers, each with its own magnet

detector:pierre-auger-observatory.name: Pierre Auger Observatory hybrid detector

description: Array of 1660 water-Cherenkov detector tanks spread over 3000 km^2, sampling the particle density of extensive air showers at ground level.
subsystems.name: Surface Detector (SD)

description: 27 optical telescopes in four buildings overlooking the surface array, imaging the ultraviolet fluorescence light emitted by nitrogen molecules excited along an air shower's path through the atmosphere.
subsystems.name: Fluorescence Detector (FD)

summary.plain: A two-in-one detector: 1660 tanks of water spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particles from cosmic-ray showers reaching the ground, while 27 telescopes watch the same showers develop as faint ultraviolet flashes in the night sky.

detector:pierre-auger-observatory.technology: Hybrid detector: a surface array of water-Cherenkov tanks sampling air-shower particles at ground level, cross-checked by fluorescence telescopes imaging ultraviolet light from the shower's longitudinal development.

detector:project-8.name: Project 8 CRES apparatus

summary.plain: A small tabletop instrument built at the University of Washington that catches the faint radio hum a single electron makes as it spirals in a magnetic field, the first step toward weighing the neutrino this way.

detector:project-8.technology: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES): single-electron microwave radiometry in a magnetic trap

intervals.label: construction and operation at the CERN Neutrino Platform

detector:protodune-dp.name: ProtoDUNE-DP

summary.plain: The second DUNE prototype at CERN. It tested a design in which the electron signal is amplified in a thin layer of argon gas above the liquid, allowing a much longer drift.

detector:protodune-dp.technology: dual-phase liquid argon time projection chamber with a single homogeneous drift volume and charge amplification in the gas phase

intervals.label: operation at the CERN Neutrino Platform

detector:protodune-sp.name: ProtoDUNE-SP

subsystems.description: Full-size DUNE APAs, three per anode plane, reading out the two drift volumes
subsystems.name: Anode plane assemblies

subsystems.description: External cosmic-ray tagger used together with the beam instrumentation
subsystems.name: Cosmic-ray tagger

summary.plain: A full-height prototype of the DUNE far detector, built at CERN and exposed to a test beam of known particles from 2018. It showed that the design works before the real detectors were built in South Dakota.

detector:protodune-sp.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber, a full-height prototype of the DUNE single-phase far detector module

detector:reno.name: RENO detectors

summary.plain: Two identical tank-like detectors near and far from South Korea's Hanbit nuclear reactors, watching for antineutrinos. Data taking ran from 2011 to 2023.

detector:reno.technology: Two identical gadolinium-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors

detector:ricochet-cryocube.name: Ricochet CryoCube (Ge/Zn cryogenic calorimeter array)

target_mass.display: 126 g (3 x 42 g Ge, mini-CryoCube commissioning module)

summary.plain: A set of ultra-cold germanium and zinc crystals, weighing from a few dozen grams (in the test module now running) up to a planned kilogram scale, designed to catch reactor antineutrinos nudging whole atomic nuclei.

detector:ricochet-cryocube.technology: cryogenic heat-and-ionization germanium and zinc calorimeters (CryoCube)

detector:rno-g.name: RNO-G stations

subsystems.description: Three strings of 15 antennas per station, ~100 m below the surface
subsystems.name: Deep strings

subsystems.description: 9 surface antennas per station
subsystems.name: Surface antennas

summary.plain: Stations of buried and surface radio antennas, spaced more than a kilometre apart on the Greenland ice sheet, listening for the radio crackle of the highest-energy neutrinos.

detector:rno-g.technology: In-ice radio antenna stations: each with three strings of antennas ~100 m deep in the firn plus surface antennas, detecting the Askaryan radio pulse from neutrino-induced showers in ice

detector:sage.name: SAGE gallium target

summary.plain: Tonnes of liquid gallium metal, deep in a Russian mountain, that solar neutrinos occasionally turn into germanium, which scientists then extract and count.

detector:sage.technology: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge via inverse beta decay in liquid gallium metal, which is chemically extracted and counted in periodic campaigns

detector:sbnd.name: SBND detector

summary.plain: A 112-tonne liquid argon camera only 110 metres from where Fermilab makes its Booster neutrino beam. Being so close, it sees about 7,000 neutrinos a day, more than any similar detector.

detector:sbnd.technology: single-phase liquid argon time projection chamber

detector:seaquest.name: SeaQuest spectrometer

summary.plain: The SeaQuest spectrometer used magnets and tracking detectors to catch pairs of muons produced when a proton beam struck hydrogen, deuterium and other targets, revealing the makeup of the proton's antiquark sea.

detector:seaquest.technology: Muon spectrometer: a target system followed by two dipole magnets and four detector stations (hodoscopes and tracking chambers) with an FPGA-based trigger, identifying oppositely-charged dimuon pairs from the Drell-Yan process

detector:sensei.name: SENSEI Skipper-CCD detector

summary.plain: A tiny silicon chip called a skipper CCD, sensitive enough to count single electrons, sitting in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab to catch the faint signal of a very light dark matter particle.

detector:sensei.technology: Skipper charge-coupled device (CCD): a high-resistivity silicon CCD with sub-electron readout noise, counting individual ionization electrons

detector:ship.name: SHiP detector

summary.plain: The planned SHiP detector: a beam-dump target, a muon shield, an empty decay volume, and a spectrometer, built to catch the decays of hypothetical new particles that could otherwise pass through matter unnoticed.

detector:ship.technology: High-intensity proton beam-dump on a heavy target, followed by a muon shield, a large vacuum decay volume and a downstream spectrometer/calorimeter system to reconstruct decays of feebly interacting long-lived particles

detector:sld.name: SLD detector

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC built around the collision point of the SLC accelerator, with a precise silicon vertex detector and a ring-imaging Cherenkov detector to identify particle types.

detector:sld.technology: CCD pixel vertex detector, drift-chamber tracking, Cherenkov ring-imaging particle identification, projective-tower calorimetry and a muon tracking system

detector:snd-lhc.name: SND@LHC detector

summary.plain: The SND@LHC detector sits in a disused CERN tunnel opposite FASER, built to catch neutrinos and rare particles from LHC collisions. It operated from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.

detector:snd-lhc.technology: Hybrid emulsion/electronic-tracker target (tungsten plates) acting as an electromagnetic calorimeter, followed by a hadronic calorimeter and a muon identification system

detector:sno.name: SNO detector

description: An array of proportional counters strung through the heavy water in phase 3 to independently detect the neutral-current reaction via neutron capture
subsystems.name: Neutral Current Detector (NCD) array

summary.plain: A 12-metre acrylic ball full of heavy water, watched by 9,600 light sensors, sitting two kilometres underground in a Canadian mine.
