detector:veritas.name: VERITAS telescope array

summary.plain: Four 12-metre dish telescopes on a mountaintop that catch the flicker of blue light made when gamma rays hit the upper atmosphere.

detector:veritas.technology: Array of four 12 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes.

detector:xenon1t.name: XENON1T detector

summary.plain: A tank of 3.2 tonnes of liquid xenon, 2 tonnes of it actively watched, that recorded flashes of light from particles bumping into xenon atoms deep under an Italian mountain.

detector:xenon1t.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid xenon time projection chamber

detector:xenonnt.name: XENONnT detector

summary.plain: A tank of nearly six tonnes of liquid xenon, watched by light sensors, that records the tiny flash made if a dark matter particle -- or a neutrino -- bumps into a xenon atom. It is the enlarged, cleaner successor to the XENON1T detector, in the same underground hall in Italy.

detector:xenonnt.technology: dual-phase (two-phase) liquid xenon time projection chamber

detector:zeus.name: ZEUS detector

summary.plain: A large detector at DESY, built around one of the two points on the HERA ring where electrons and protons collided, using a dense uranium calorimeter to measure particle energies very precisely.

detector:zeus.technology: Compensating uranium-scintillator calorimeter with central and forward/backward silicon and drift/straw-tube tracking in a superconducting solenoid, plus an instrumented-iron muon system

aliases: A Broadband/Resonant Approach to Cosmic Axion Detection with an Amplifying B-field Ring Apparatus
experiment:abracadabra.name: ABRACADABRA

summary.plain: ABRACADABRA-10 cm was a small prototype at MIT that searched for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, using a toroidal magnet instead of the resonant cavities other experiments use. Its axion search finished around 2021.

ADMX searches for the axion, a hypothetical particle that could make up dark matter. At the University of Washington, a tunable metal cavity sits inside a powerful magnet, hunting for a faint microwave signal that dark-matter axions would produce.

experiment:aleph.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 200 GeV from 1995)
experiment:aleph.name: ALEPH

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, used to study the Z and W bosons with great precision, including proving there are exactly three kinds of light neutrino.

experiment:alice.energy_regime: Pb-Pb (and other heavy-ion) collisions at up to 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair; p-Pb collisions; pp reference collisions at LHC energies (up to 13.6 TeV in Run 3)
experiment:alice.name: ALICE

summary.plain: ALICE is CERN's dedicated heavy-ion experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. By colliding lead nuclei instead of protons, it recreates the quark-gluon plasma, an extremely hot and dense state of matter thought to have filled the universe microseconds after the Big Bang, and studies how ordinary matter freezes out of it.

intervals.label: Technical Design Report submitted to DESY PRC

summary.plain: ALPS II shines a laser at a light-tight wall to see whether a tiny fraction can pass through as an undetectable particle and turn back into light on the far side. This would reveal new, very light particles related to dark matter. It has been operating at DESY since 2023.

aliases: Antarctic Muon and Neutrino Detector Array
experiment:amanda.energy_regime: Atmospheric and astrophysical neutrinos with typical reconstructed energies of several hundred GeV and above
experiment:amanda.name: AMANDA

summary.plain: The pioneering telescope that froze light sensors into the ice at the South Pole to catch neutrinos. It proved the idea worked and was later absorbed into its much bigger successor, IceCube.

A radio antenna array flown high over Antarctica on a NASA balloon, using the entire ice sheet below as a giant listening surface for ultra-high-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays. It flew five times between 2003 and 2016.

aliases: Astronomy with a Neutrino Telescope and Abyss environmental RESearch
experiment:antares.name: ANTARES

summary.plain: The first neutrino telescope built under the sea. For sixteen years, twelve long cables of light sensors hung nearly 2.5 kilometres deep in the Mediterranean off Toulon, France, watching for the faint blue flashes that a neutrino from space can make.
A handful of radio-antenna stations buried in the ice near the South Pole, testing technology for finding the highest-energy neutrinos from space and for a future upgrade to IceCube.

aliases: Antarctic Ross Ice Shelf Antenna Neutrino Array

key_specs.label: Ice shelf thickness at deployment site

experiment:arianna.name: ARIANNA

summary.plain: A small, now-shut-down array of radio antennas that once sat on the surface of Antarctica's Ross Ice Shelf, listening for the crackle of ultra-high-energy neutrinos, and testing ideas for a much bigger array that was never built.

experiment:atlas.energy_regime: Proton-proton collisions at 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy; lead-lead collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair
experiment:atlas.name: ATLAS

summary.plain: ATLAS is one of the two big general-purpose experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Its 7000-tonne detector sits in a cavern 100 metres underground and records what comes out of proton collisions. In 2012 ATLAS and CMS announced the discovery of the Higgs boson.

experiment:babar.energy_regime: Asymmetric e+e- collisions at 10.58 GeV center-of-mass (the Upsilon(4S) resonance)
experiment:babar.name: BaBar

summary.plain: A particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, built to study why matter and antimatter behave slightly differently by watching B mesons decay. It ran from 1999 to 2008 and, together with Japan's Belle experiment, confirmed a theory that won the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.
A growing underwater telescope in Lake Baikal, Siberia, that has been adding new clusters of light sensors every year since 2016 in search of neutrinos from deep space.

experiment:belle.energy_regime: e+e- collisions at the Υ(4S) resonance, √s ≈ 10.58 GeV
experiment:belle.name: Belle

summary.plain: An experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan that ran from 1999 to 2010. It watched electrons and positrons collide to make pairs of B particles, and showed that matter and antimatter behave differently — work that led to the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.

The successor to the Belle experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan. Running since 2019, it records electron-positron collisions from the SuperKEKB machine, looking for tiny departures from the known laws of physics in the decays of heavy, short-lived particles.

A giant ball of ultra-pure liquid deep under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy that directly watched low-energy neutrinos streaming from the Sun's core, including two kinds no one had ever seen before.

CAST looked for axions, hypothetical particles that might explain dark matter, by pointing a powerful magnet left over from Large Hadron Collider testing at the Sun and watching for X-rays. It ran at CERN from 2003 until the end of 2022.

intervals.label: first Tevatron proton-antiproton collisions observed by CDF
engineering run and first physics results

summary.plain: A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, that watched protons and their antimatter twins smash together at nearly the speed of light. It helped find the top quark, the heaviest known building block of matter, and ran until the Tevatron collider it depended on shut down in 2011.

experiment:cdms-ii.energy_regime: keV-scale nuclear recoils, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent limit quoted near 70 GeV/c^2 WIMP mass
experiment:cdms-ii.name: CDMS II

summary.plain: CDMS II searched for dark matter particles using very cold germanium and silicon crystals half a mile underground in Minnesota. It ran from about 2005 to 2009 and found no convincing signal, but set some of the tightest limits of its time on how often dark matter might bump into ordinary atoms.

experiment:cms.energy_regime: Proton-proton (and heavy-ion) collisions at TeV centre-of-mass energies: designed for 14 TeV, 13.6 TeV delivered in LHC Run 3
experiment:cms.name: CMS

summary.plain: One of the two big general-purpose experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Thousands of scientists use it to photograph the debris of proton collisions 40 million times a second. In 2012 it was one of the two experiments that found the Higgs boson.

key_specs.label: CsI[Na] detector baseline (distance from neutrino source)

summary.plain: An experiment at a US national laboratory that catches neutrinos from a neutron-making machine and watches them bounce gently off whole atomic nuclei, a process predicted for decades but only directly seen for the first time in 2017.

key_specs.label: Phase-I sensitivity goal (90% C.L. upper limit)

summary.plain: An experiment being built at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan to look for a muon turning directly into an electron near an aluminium atom -- a process the Standard Model forbids. It is being built in stages, starting with a smaller first phase.

key_specs.label: Distance from reactor core (Leibstadt / CONUS+ phase)

summary.plain: A small, sensitive detector using ultra-pure germanium crystals to catch reactor antineutrinos gently bouncing off whole atomic nuclei, first run at a German nuclear plant and, after it closed, moved to a Swiss one under the name CONUS+.

aliases: Cryogenic Rare Event Search with Superconducting Thermometers
experiment:cresst.energy_regime: Sub-GeV WIMPs; CRESST-III reaches nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower, probing masses down to ~70 MeV/c^2

intervals.label: CRESST-I: construction and first run (sapphire detectors)

experiment:cresst.name: CRESST

summary.plain: CRESST looks for dark matter using crystals of calcium tungstate, cooled to a whisker above absolute zero deep under an Italian mountain. Each tiny bump from a passing particle makes both heat and a flash of light, and comparing the two tells physicists what kind of particle caused it.

A next-generation gamma-ray observatory being built at two sites, one in Spain and one in Chile, using dozens of telescopes of three different sizes to see the whole sky and the widest range of gamma-ray energies of any single project.

aliases: Cryogenic Underground Observatory for Rare Events
experiment:cuore.name: CUORE

summary.plain: A huge array of super-cold tellurium crystals under an Italian mountain, listening for a faint click of heat that would signal a rare radioactive decay. CUORE has been steadily collecting data since 2019.

The planned successor to CUORE: about 1500 crystals of a different material (lithium molybdate) that both glow and register heat, reusing CUORE's giant refrigerator under an Italian mountain to search for a rare radioactive process even more precisely.

A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, named after its position on the Tevatron collider ring. It watched protons and antiprotons collide from 1992 until the Tevatron shut down in 2011, and it co-discovered the top quark in 1995.

experiment:damic.energy_regime: WIMPs of a few GeV/c^2 (silicon target); low-energy ionization excess near 100 eV under continued study

intervals.label: SNOLAB: repurposed as background test stand

quantity.display: 7 x 16-Mpixel CCDs, 6.0 g each (~42 g total)

experiment:damic.name: DAMIC

summary.plain: DAMIC searched for dark matter using the same kind of light-sensing chips found in digital cameras, cooled and shielded deep underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It started at Fermilab and moved to SNOLAB, later gaining even more sensitive 'skipper' chips, before the detector was repurposed as a background test stand around 2025.

aliases: DArk Matter In CCDs at Modane
experiment:damic-m.energy_regime: Hidden-sector / light dark matter, roughly 0.5-1000 MeV/c^2 (electron-recoil channel)

intervals.label: Low Background Chamber: status and first results

experiment:damic-m.name: DAMIC-M

summary.plain: DAMIC-M is the next generation of the DAMIC dark matter search, using very sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs that can count single electrons. A 20-gram prototype has been running deep under a mountain in the French Alps since 2022, hunting for very light, hidden particles.

DarkQuest is a proposed Fermilab experiment that would reuse the SeaQuest particle detector to search for hidden, dark-sector particles instead of ordinary quarks, at low cost since it builds on equipment already installed.

DarkSide-20k will be a much bigger dark matter detector, holding fifty tonnes of liquid argon, being built deep under a mountain in Italy. It is the successor of the smaller DarkSide-50 experiment and is still under construction, with data taking expected around 2026-2027.

DarkSide-50 was a dark matter detector holding fifty kilograms of liquid argon, deep under a mountain in Italy. It ran from 2013 to 2020, testing techniques later scaled up for its successor, DarkSide-20k.

intervals.label: seven-AD configuration (one AD re-purposed for JUNO-related R&D)

summary.plain: An experiment in southern China that used clusters of detectors near and far from nuclear reactors to discover that one type of neutrino oscillation, long searched for, really happens.

aliases: Dark matter Experiment using Argon Pulse-shape discrimination
experiment:deap-3600.name: DEAP-3600

summary.plain: DEAP-3600 is a dark matter experiment 2 km underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It watches 3.6 tonnes of liquid argon for the faint flash of light a dark matter particle would make hitting an argon nucleus. It has taken data since late 2016 and is currently being upgraded for a further run.

aliases: Detector with Lepton, Photon and Hadron Identification
experiment:delphi.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)
experiment:delphi.name: DELPHI

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, known for its Ring Imaging Cherenkov detectors that could identify the type of each charged particle produced.

DMRadio is a series of experiments at Stanford and SLAC that search for very light dark-matter axions using a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit instead of a microwave cavity. It is currently being built.

aliases: Direct Observation of the NU Tau
experiment:donut.energy_regime: Tau neutrinos from charmed-meson decay in a Tevatron fixed-target proton beam dump
experiment:donut.name: DONUT

summary.plain: A Fermilab experiment that ran for a few months in 1997, aiming a proton beam from the Tevatron at a target to make tau neutrinos and catching them directly for the first time in stacks of photographic emulsion, completing the direct detection of every particle the Standard Model predicts.

intervals.label: near and far detectors both operating

summary.plain: A French experiment that watched antineutrinos from the Chooz nuclear reactors with two detectors at different distances, finding evidence that they change type on the way.

experiment:dune.energy_regime: GeV-scale accelerator neutrinos (wide band, 60-120 GeV protons), plus MeV-scale supernova neutrinos

intervals.label: DUNE collaboration formed from LBNE and LBNO

experiment:dune.name: Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment

summary.plain: A very large experiment that will send neutrinos 1285 kilometres through the Earth from Illinois to South Dakota, where detectors filled with liquid argon a mile underground will record them. It aims to find out whether neutrinos and antineutrinos behave differently, to catch neutrinos from an exploding star, and to look for protons decaying.

E949 was a Brookhaven National Laboratory experiment that stopped kaons in a detector to catch the same ultra-rare decay NA62 studies today -- a kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos -- continuing the earlier E787 experiment.

aliases: Experience pour DEtecter Les WIMPs En Site Souterrain
experiment:edelweiss.energy_regime: Sub-GeV dark matter (32-100 MeV/c^2 via the Migdal effect) and traditional WIMP masses via nuclear recoils

experiment:edelweiss.name: EDELWEISS

summary.plain: EDELWEISS searches for dark matter using pure germanium crystals cooled to near absolute zero, deep under a mountain in the French Alps. Recent versions are sensitive enough to look for dark matter far lighter than a proton.
A liquid-xenon detector buried deep in a New Mexico salt mine that also stores nuclear waste. EXO-200 searched for a rare radioactive process in xenon atoms from 2011 to 2018 and found no signal.

experiment:faser.energy_regime: LHC Run 3 proton-proton collisions at 13.6 TeV, sampled via forward particle flux along the beam axis
experiment:faser.name: FASER

summary.plain: FASER is a small experiment placed in an unused tunnel 480 metres from CERN's ATLAS detector, watching for rare, long-lived particles and neutrinos that fly straight down the LHC's beamline.
An experiment in an Italian mountain lab that used tonnes of liquid gallium to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos, the ones from its very first fusion step.

A neutrino experiment buried under a mountain in Italy that searched for a rare radioactive process in germanium atoms. Finding it would prove neutrinos are their own antiparticles. GERDA ran from 2011 to 2019 and found no signal, only setting a limit.

aliases: Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection

intervals.label: GRANDProto300 prototype deployed and taking data

experiment:grand.name: GRAND

summary.plain: A giant planned array of 200,000 radio antennas spread over a huge area, designed to catch the radio flash from ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos. Small test versions are already up and running in China, France and Argentina.

Five telescopes on a Namibian farm that watch the southern sky for gamma rays: four medium telescopes plus one giant 28-metre telescope, the largest of its kind, run by scientists from more than a dozen countries.

A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down in 2007.
A gamma-ray observatory on a Mexican volcano: an array of water tanks 4100 metres up that watches nearly the whole sky at once for the highest-energy light in the universe, day and night.

aliases: Haloscope At Yale Sensitive To Axion CDM

experiment:haystac.name: HAYSTAC

summary.plain: HAYSTAC searches for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, at Yale University. A tunable metal cavity inside a strong magnet, cooled and read out with quantum-noise-reducing electronics, listens for a faint radio signal the axion would produce.

A tank of dry-cleaning fluid nearly a mile underground in a South Dakota gold mine, run for decades by Ray Davis, that made the first direct detection of solar neutrinos and found far fewer than expected — a puzzle not solved for thirty years.

The next, much bigger version of Super-Kamiokande, being built in a newly dug cavern near the original detector. When it starts up later this decade it will use the same J-PARC neutrino beam and look for a difference between how neutrinos and antineutrinos behave, hunt for proton decay, and watch for supernovae.

IAXO is a planned next-generation axion helioscope at DESY, a much larger successor to CAST. Its intermediate prototype, BabyIAXO, is currently under construction, while the full-scale instrument remains a proposal.

The first big liquid-argon neutrino detector ever built. It ran under an Italian mountain from 2010-2013, was rebuilt at CERN, and now sits at Fermilab as the far detector in a hunt for a possible fourth kind of neutrino.

experiment:icecube.energy_regime: About 10 GeV (DeepCore threshold) to the PeV scale and above for in-ice neutrinos; 300 TeV to 1 EeV cosmic rays with IceTop
experiment:icecube.name: IceCube

summary.plain: A cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice at the South Pole turned into a telescope. More than five thousand light sensors frozen deep in the ice catch the faint flashes made when a neutrino from space crashes into the ice.

The planned successor to IceCube: about eight times the volume of ice, ten thousand light sensors and a huge radio antenna array, designed to catch many more neutrinos and the most energetic ones of all.

New, more sensitive light detectors added to the middle of IceCube. They let the observatory see lower-energy neutrinos more sharply and help scientists understand the ice itself, which improves every measurement IceCube has already made.

final construction stage: water and liquid-scintillator filling

summary.plain: A giant underground detector in southern China that studies neutrinos from nearby nuclear power reactors. It began taking data in 2025 and aims to work out the ordering of neutrino masses and measure their oscillations with world-leading precision.

aliases: KEK to Kamioka long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment
experiment:k2k.name: K2K (KEK to Kamioka)

summary.plain: The world's first long-baseline neutrino experiment: a beam of neutrinos made at KEK's proton accelerator was sent 250 km through the Earth to the Super-Kamiokande detector, to check whether the atmospheric neutrino puzzle Super-K had already seen was really neutrino oscillation.

quantity.display: 4500 t total (680-1040 t fiducial, depending on analysis)

summary.plain: A tank of water deep in a Japanese mine, built in 1983 to look for protons decaying. It never saw one, but in February 1987 it caught a handful of neutrinos from a supernova exploding in a nearby galaxy - the first time anyone had detected neutrinos from a star other than the Sun.

intervals.label: first-results exposure used in the 2002 discovery paper

summary.plain: A huge detector in a Japanese mine that watches antineutrinos from nuclear power plants across the country, and in 2002 gave the first direct proof that they disappear the way solar-neutrino theories predicted.

aliases: Kamioka Liquid-scintillator Anti-Neutrino Detector Zero-neutrino double-beta decay search
experiment:kamland-zen.name: KamLAND-Zen

summary.plain: A xenon-loaded balloon of liquid suspended inside the KamLAND detector deep under a Japanese mountain, searching for a rare radioactive process in xenon atoms. Its latest result sets one of the strongest limits yet on the process.

aliases: KArlsruhe Rutherford Medium Energy Neutrino experiment
experiment:karmen.energy_regime: Stopped-pion/muon-decay neutrinos from an 800 MeV proton beam stop (few tens of MeV neutrino energies)

intervals.label: outer veto installation / start of KARMEN 2

experiment:karmen.name: KARMEN

summary.plain: A neutrino experiment at the ISIS particle accelerator in England, running from 1990 to 2001. A tank of liquid holding light sensors sat 18 metres from where the beam stopped, watching for neutrinos changing type on the way. It found no such change and helped test a puzzling result from a similar experiment in the United States.

A giant spectrometer in Germany that weighs neutrinos indirectly, by measuring electrons released when radioactive tritium decays. Its latest result shows the neutrino weighs no more than 0.45 electron-volts.

An experiment using two neutrino telescopes built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea, one off Sicily and one off France, to catch faint flashes of light from neutrinos arriving from space and from Earth's atmosphere.

KOTO is a Japanese experiment at J-PARC that watches for an extremely rare kaon decay into a neutral pion and two invisible neutrinos, testing the same physics as NA62 but with the neutral, longer-lived kind of kaon.

KTeV was a Fermilab experiment in the 1990s that studied neutral kaon decays, showing that nature's matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) can happen directly inside a kaon's decay, at the same time as CERN's NA48 was making the same discovery.

experiment:l3.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)
experiment:l3.name: L3

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision using bismuth-germanate crystals and a huge magnet.

aliases: Large Enriched Germanium Experiment for Neutrinoless ββ Decay
experiment:legend.name: LEGEND

summary.plain: LEGEND combines the expertise of two earlier experiments, GERDA and the Majorana Demonstrator, to search for a rare radioactive process in germanium atoms deep under an Italian mountain. Its first stage, LEGEND-200, began taking data in 2023; a larger stage, LEGEND-1000, is planned.

aliases: Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory
experiment:lhaaso.name: LHAASO

summary.plain: A high-altitude Chinese observatory that measures cosmic rays and hunts for the highest-energy gamma rays in the sky, using several kinds of detectors together on a mountain 4410 metres up.

experiment:lhcb.energy_regime: Proton-proton collisions at 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy at the LHC, plus heavy-ion and fixed-target (SMOG) running

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 2 / LHCb Upgrade I installation

experiment:lhcb.name: LHCb

summary.plain: LHCb is one of the four big experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Instead of surrounding the collision point on all sides, its detector is shaped like a single forward cone, built to catch particles containing beauty and charm quarks and study why the universe has so much more matter than antimatter.

experiment:lhcf.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton (and light-ion) collisions, run mainly during early low-luminosity periods of each LHC run
experiment:lhcf.name: LHCf

summary.plain: LHCf uses two small detectors, 140 metres either side of CERN's ATLAS collision point, to study particles thrown almost exactly forward by LHC collisions -- data used to help interpret how cosmic rays create showers when they hit Earth's atmosphere.

experiment:lsnd.energy_regime: Stopped-pion/muon-decay neutrinos from an 800 MeV LAMPF/LANSCE proton beam
experiment:lsnd.name: LSND

summary.plain: A tank of mineral oil at Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico, that watched for neutrinos changing type just 30 metres from where an accelerator beam produced them. From 1993 to 1998 it reported more electron-antineutrinos than expected, a puzzling result that later experiments tried to confirm or rule out.

LUX was a dark matter detector holding about a third of a tonne of liquid xenon, run from 2013 to 2016 in the same underground hall in South Dakota that LZ uses now. It found no dark matter, and set the tightest limits of its day.

experiment:lz.energy_regime: keV-scale nuclear recoils from WIMPs of a few GeV/c2 to hundreds of TeV/c2
experiment:lz.name: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ)

summary.plain: LZ is a dark matter experiment a mile underground in South Dakota. It watches seven tonnes of liquid xenon for the tiny flash of light expected if a dark matter particle hits a xenon nucleus. It began taking data at the end of 2021 and has seen no such particle so far.

aliases: Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes
experiment:magic.name: MAGIC

summary.plain: Two 17-metre telescopes on a mountain in the Canary Islands that catch the faint blue flashes gamma rays make when they hit the atmosphere.

A demonstration experiment nearly a mile underground in a former South Dakota gold mine, using germanium crystals to search for a rare radioactive process. It proved the low-background techniques later scaled up in the LEGEND experiment.

aliases: MAssive Timing Hodoscope for Ultra Stable neutraL pArticles

quantity.display: 11 m tall (proposed 40 m x 40 m x 11 m decay volume)

experiment:mathusla.name: MATHUSLA

summary.plain: MATHUSLA is a proposed detector that would sit on the surface at CERN, far above the LHC's underground collisions, to catch new particles so weakly interacting and long-lived that they could fly through ordinary detectors unnoticed.

An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute in Switzerland that looked for a muon turning directly into an electron and a burst of light -- a decay the Standard Model forbids. It ran from 2009 to 2013 and did not see the decay, setting a new best limit.
The upgraded version of MEG at the same Swiss laboratory, hunting for the same forbidden muon decay with about ten times better sensitivity. It has been taking data since 2021 and is still running.

A 170-tonne liquid-argon camera on Fermilab's Booster neutrino beam, built to find out what caused an earlier experiment's mysterious signal, and along the way to measure neutrino collisions with unprecedented clarity.
A compact, finely sliced detector at Fermilab that measured exactly how neutrinos bounce off different atomic nuclei, data that other neutrino experiments need to interpret their own results.

A Fermilab experiment built to settle a puzzling result from an earlier Los Alamos experiment. It watched a beam of neutrinos with a 12-metre sphere of mineral oil from 2002 to 2019, and saw its own unexplained excess of signals.

experiment:minos.energy_regime: On-axis NuMI νμ-dominated beam, peak energy about 3 GeV
experiment:minos.name: MINOS

summary.plain: A neutrino experiment that sent Fermilab's beam 735 kilometres underground to an old iron mine in Minnesota, comparing what arrived to what was measured near the source, from 2005 to 2012.
MINOS's second act: the same two detectors kept running from 2013 to 2016 on a higher-energy beam, hunting for a hypothetical fourth kind of neutrino.

aliases: Monopole and Exotics Detector at the LHC
Monopole and Exotic Particle Detector at the LHC
experiment:moedal.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton (and heavy-ion) collisions at Point 8, 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:moedal.name: MoEDAL

summary.plain: MoEDAL is an unusual CERN experiment that mostly just sits there: sheets of plastic and jars of special metal quietly record the trails of exotic, heavily-charged particles -- like magnetic monopoles -- that might be created in LHC collisions at the LHCb cavern.

intervals.label: DOE CD-3 construction approval and construction

summary.plain: An experiment being built at Fermilab that will look for a muon turning directly into an electron without any neutrinos -- something the standard laws of particle physics say should never happen. Construction is under way; no data has been taken yet.

An experiment being built at the Paul Scherrer Institute in Switzerland to look for a muon splitting into three lighter particles (two positrons and an electron), which the Standard Model says essentially never happens. It is still under construction.

intervals.label: storage ring relocated from BNL and reassembled at Fermilab (MC-1)

summary.plain: An experiment at Fermilab that stores muons in a 14-metre magnetic ring and watches them wobble, to measure one of their properties (called g-2) more precisely than ever and test whether unknown particles are secretly tugging on it.

intervals.label: NA48 main run (direct CP violation, KL/KS beams)
NA48/2 (charged-kaon CP violation and rare decays)

summary.plain: NA48 was a CERN experiment that ran from the late 1990s to the mid-2000s, confirming that nature's matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) can arise directly inside a kaon's decay, not just from how kaons mix. It was the direct predecessor of NA62 at the same underground cavern.

intervals.label: long shutdown / detector upgrades before Run 2

summary.plain: NA62 is a CERN experiment that fires a beam of charged kaons at a detector to catch one of the rarest particle decays known: a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos. Catching enough of these decays tests the Standard Model.

NA64 is a CERN experiment that fires an electron beam into a block of material and watches for missing energy -- a sign that an invisible, unknown particle escaped. It searches for dark photons and other hidden particles.

NEWS-G hunts for very light dark matter particles using a large hollow copper ball filled with gas, deep underground. A small 60 cm version ran in France; a bigger 135 cm sphere has been running at SNOLAB in Canada since 2021.

A planned successor to EXO-200: a much bigger liquid-xenon detector, holding five tonnes of xenon, proposed for the SNOLAB underground laboratory in Canada. It would search for the same rare radioactive process, with far greater sensitivity.

aliases: Neutrino Experiment with a Xenon TPC
experiment:next.name: NEXT

summary.plain: A detector at an underground laboratory in the Spanish Pyrenees that uses high-pressure xenon gas, rather than liquid, to search for a rare radioactive process. Its main detector, NEXT-100, started running in 2024.

experiment:nova.energy_regime: Off-axis NuMI wide-band beam peaked at 1.8 GeV
experiment:nova.name: NOvA

summary.plain: A long-distance neutrino experiment: Fermilab fires a beam of neutrinos 810 kilometres through the Earth to northern Minnesota, watching how they change type on the way to learn about neutrino masses and matter-antimatter asymmetry.
A very small, super-cold detector at a French nuclear power plant, sitting closer to the reactor core than any similar experiment, built to catch antineutrinos at the gentlest nudges ever attempted.

experiment:opal.energy_regime: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)

quantity.display: ~12 m long x 12 m high x 12 m wide

experiment:opal.name: OPAL

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, built as a layered, general-purpose apparatus about the size of a house to catch every kind of particle from the collisions.

experiment:opera.energy_regime: GeV-scale muon-neutrino beam from SPS protons on a graphite target (CNGS)
experiment:opera.name: OPERA

summary.plain: An experiment in a mountain tunnel in Italy that caught neutrinos fired 732 kilometres through the Earth from CERN in Switzerland. Its photographic-film-and-lead detector directly caught tau neutrinos appearing from a beam that started as muon neutrinos, proving they change type over the trip.

intervals.label: pathfinder programme deployed and taking data (STRAW active; P-ONE-1 integrated/tested, first line not yet deployed)

summary.plain: A planned neutrino telescope for the deep Pacific Ocean off Canada's west coast, building on an undersea science network. A small pathfinder instrument has been actively taking data there since 2019, proving the technology, while the full telescope and its first production line are still being built.

aliases: Particle and Astrophysical Xenon Detector 4 Ton
experiment:pandax-4t.name: PandaX-4T

summary.plain: PandaX-4T is a dark matter detector holding four tonnes of liquid xenon, deep under a mountain at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. It has been taking data since 2021, searching for dark matter particles bumping into xenon nuclei.

aliases: Pioneering High Energy Nuclear Interaction eXperiment
experiment:phenix.name: PHENIX

summary.plain: PHENIX was one of the two large experiments at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built from four merged detector proposals to study hot nuclear matter. It recorded its first collision in 2000 and stopped taking data in 2016.

A giant hybrid detector in Argentina that catches the rarest, most energetic cosmic rays known: water tanks spread over 3000 square kilometres sense particle showers at ground level while telescopes watch the sky for their faint ultraviolet glow.

intervals.label: Phase I: CRES demonstration (University of Washington)
Phase II: first CRES measurement of molecular tritium

summary.plain: An experiment that measures the faint radio signal a single electron gives off when it spins in a magnetic field, aiming to weigh the neutrino. It began as a tabletop demonstration at the University of Washington and is now moving toward using real tritium gas.

A South Korean experiment with two identical detectors near and far from a group of six nuclear reactors, which observed antineutrinos disappearing exactly as neutrino oscillation theory predicts. Data taking ran from 2011 to 2023.

A reactor-neutrino experiment at a French research reactor, using ultra-cold germanium and zinc crystals just a few metres from the reactor core to catch antineutrinos bouncing off whole atomic nuclei.
A radio-antenna neutrino detector being built into the ice at the very top of Greenland's ice sheet, one station at a time, to catch the radio flash from the highest-energy neutrinos from space.
An experiment deep inside a Russian mountain that uses tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos.

The newest and closest of Fermilab's three short-baseline liquid-argon detectors, sitting right next to where the neutrino beam is made so it can measure the beam before anything has a chance to change.

SeaQuest was a Fermilab experiment that fired a proton beam at hydrogen and deuterium targets to measure how down and up antiquarks are distributed differently inside a proton, finishing its analysis in 2025.

experiment:sensei.energy_regime: Sub-GeV dark matter via electron recoils (roughly 500 keV to a few GeV in mass)

intervals.label: science operations at Fermilab MINOS cavern

experiment:sensei.name: SENSEI

summary.plain: SENSEI uses ultra-sensitive silicon chips called skipper CCDs to hunt for very light dark matter particles, so light that they would only knock loose a handful of electrons. It has run in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab near Chicago since 2018.

intervals.label: SPSC review of Technical and Physics Proposal

summary.plain: SHiP is a planned CERN experiment that will dump an intense proton beam into a heavy target and search the debris for new, weakly interacting particles that could explain dark matter and other mysteries. It is approved to be built in the same underground hall once used by NA48 and NA62.

intervals.label: final checkout on the SLC beamline

summary.plain: A general-purpose particle detector at SLAC, near Stanford, California, that used a uniquely highly polarized electron beam to make some of the most precise measurements of how the Z boson decays. It ran from 1991 to 1998.

experiment:snd-lhc.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton collisions (Run 3, 13.6 TeV), sampled via very-forward particle flux
experiment:snd-lhc.name: SND@LHC

summary.plain: SND@LHC is a compact experiment in a disused CERN tunnel that catches neutrinos produced in LHC collisions, in a direction close to the beam that no other LHC experiment can see. It recorded collision data from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.

intervals.label: detector construction (clean room, acrylic vessel, PMT support, water fill)

summary.plain: A detector two kilometres underground in a Canadian nickel mine, filled with 1000 tonnes of heavy water, that solved the decades-old mystery of the Sun's missing neutrinos by showing they change type on the way to Earth.
SNO+ reuses the same underground cavern and acrylic ball that SNO used, now filled with liquid scintillator, to search for a hypothetical nuclear decay and to study solar and reactor neutrinos.

sPHENIX is a new, house-sized detector at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built where PHENIX used to be, using a recycled magnet from the BaBar experiment to study the hot soup of quarks and gluons made in nuclear collisions.

STAR is a house-sized, 1,200-tonne particle detector at Brookhaven National Laboratory that has watched gold and other heavy atomic nuclei smash together since 2000, looking for a hot, liquid-like state of matter called the quark-gluon plasma.

intervals.label: SK-II (half PMT density after the 2001 accident)

summary.plain: A tank of 50,000 tonnes of ultra-pure water, a kilometre under a mountain near Kamioka, watched by more than eleven thousand light sensors. It caught the first solid evidence that neutrinos change type as they travel, has watched the Sun in neutrinos for decades, and is the distant target for neutrino beams fired from J-PARC.

experiment:supercdms.energy_regime: Low-mass WIMPs, smaller than about ten proton masses
experiment:supercdms.name: SuperCDMS

summary.plain: SuperCDMS SNOLAB looks for dark matter using silicon and germanium crystals cooled almost to absolute zero. It is the successor to an earlier version of the experiment that ran at the Soudan mine in Minnesota until 2015, and is now starting up nearly a mile underground at SNOLAB in Canada, aiming at very light dark matter particles.

aliases: Super Cryogenic Dark Matter Search at Soudan Mine
experiment:supercdms-soudan.name: SuperCDMS Soudan

summary.plain: The first-generation SuperCDMS dark matter detector, which ran in the Soudan mine in Minnesota from about 2009 until 2015, using an improved version of the CDMS II crystal detectors before the experiment moved to a larger site in Canada.

intervals.label: first T2K neutrino event observed at Super-Kamiokande
shutdown after the Great East Japan Earthquake
shutdown after the J-PARC hadron-hall radiation accident
T2K-II: operation with the upgraded ND280 and 760 kW beam

summary.plain: A beam of neutrinos made at the J-PARC accelerator in Tokai, on Japan's Pacific coast, is aimed 295 km across the country at the Super-Kamiokande detector under a mountain near Kamioka. By comparing what arrives with what was sent, T2K found that muon neutrinos turn into electron neutrinos, and is now comparing neutrinos with antineutrinos.

A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert with over 500 ground detectors spread across 700 square kilometres and telescopes at three stations, watching for the rarest, most energetic particles from space; recently made four times bigger by the TAx4 extension.

aliases: TOTal Elastic and diffractive cross section Measurement
Total Cross Section, Elastic Scattering and Diffraction Dissociation at the LHC
experiment:totem.energy_regime: LHC proton-proton collisions, 7-13.6 TeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:totem.name: TOTEM

summary.plain: TOTEM sits around CMS's collision point and measures protons that barely miss each other, letting physicists work out the total chance that two protons collide at all -- one of the most basic numbers in particle physics.

experiment:ua1.energy_regime: Proton-antiproton collisions at 540-630 GeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:ua1.name: UA1

summary.plain: A giant particle detector built around CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron in the early 1980s, when the machine was turned into a proton-antiproton collider. UA1 co-discovered the W and Z bosons, the carriers of the weak nuclear force.

experiment:ua2.energy_regime: Proton-antiproton collisions at 540-630 GeV centre-of-mass energy
experiment:ua2.name: UA2

summary.plain: A particle detector built around CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron in the early 1980s, alongside UA1, when the machine was turned into a proton-antiproton collider. UA2 co-discovered the W and Z bosons using precise calorimeters rather than a magnetic spectrometer.

aliases: Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System
experiment:veritas.name: VERITAS

summary.plain: Four 12-metre telescopes on a mountain in Arizona that catch the faint flashes of light made when gamma rays hit the atmosphere, letting astronomers study exploding stars, black holes and other extreme places in the universe.

XENON1T was a tank of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy that searched for dark matter particles bumping into xenon atoms. It ran from 2015 to 2018 and was for a time the most sensitive dark matter detector in the world. It is the direct predecessor of the larger XENONnT experiment now running in the same underground hall.

XENONnT is a tank of nearly six tonnes of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy, watching for dark matter particles and other rare signals. It is the upgraded successor of XENON1T, has been running since 2020, and has set new dark matter limits and reported the first hint of solar neutrinos bouncing off xenon nuclei.

A particle detector at the German laboratory DESY, in Hamburg, that watched electrons and protons collide head-on to map out what a proton is made of, and to search for new particles and forces. It ran from 1992 until HERA, the collider it depended on, shut down on 30 June 2007.

facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-stati.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
facility:amundsen-scott-south-pole-stati.operator_text: U.S. National Science Foundation / U.S. Antarctic Program

summary.plain: The United States research station at the South Pole. It is the southernmost place people live all year, and it supports the giant IceCube neutrino telescope buried in the ice below it.

facility:argonne-national-laboratory.name: Argonne National Laboratory
facility:argonne-national-laboratory.operator_text: The University of Chicago, through its subordinate UChicago Argonne LLC, for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: A United States Department of Energy multidisciplinary science laboratory near Chicago, one of the country's oldest national laboratories.

facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino.name: Baikal Deep Underwater Neutrino Telescope
facility:baikal-deep-underwater-neutrino.operator_text: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)

summary.plain: A Russian-led neutrino telescope growing year by year on the bottom of Lake Baikal, the world's deepest freshwater lake. Strings of light sensors hang beneath the ice, watching for flashes made by neutrinos from space.

facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.name: Baksan Neutrino Observatory
facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.operator: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)
facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory.operator_text: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)

summary.plain: An underground laboratory dug into a mountain in the Russian Caucasus, more than two kilometres of rock overhead, built to study neutrinos from the Sun and elsewhere.

facility:boulby-underground-laboratory.name: Boulby Underground Laboratory
facility:boulby-underground-laboratory.operator_text: STFC (Science and Technology Facilities Council), in close partnership with ICL-UK

summary.plain: A deep underground science laboratory in a working mine on the English coast, more than a kilometre below ground. It hosts dark-matter searches and other experiments that need to be shielded from cosmic rays.
A now-closed German nuclear power plant on the Elbe river that hosted the CONUS reactor-neutrino experiment from 2018 until the setup moved to Switzerland in 2023.

facility:brookhaven-national-laboratory.name: Brookhaven National Laboratory
facility:brookhaven-national-laboratory.operator_text: Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (a partnership of Stony Brook University and Battelle, with six core universities) for the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science

summary.plain: A United States national laboratory on Long Island, New York, run for the Department of Energy. It built and operated the world's first collider able to smash together beams of gold atomic nuclei and of protons with aligned spins, and it hosts other major physics, biology and materials-science facilities.

facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory.name: Laboratorio Subterraneo de Canfranc
facility:canfranc-underground-laboratory.operator_text: A Consortium of the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation, the Aragon Regional Government and the University of Zaragoza

summary.plain: An underground laboratory beneath a mountain in the Spanish Pyrenees, reached through a disused railway tunnel near Canfranc. Its 800 metres of rock shield sensitive experiments searching for dark matter and rare nuclear processes.

aliases: Organisation européenne pour la recherche nucléaire
facility:cern.name: CERN
facility:cern.operator_text: CERN, European Organization for Nuclear Research

summary.plain: CERN is Europe's particle physics laboratory, on the Swiss-French border near Geneva. Founded in 1954 by twelve countries, it builds and runs the accelerators that send beams of protons and ions into experiments such as ATLAS and CMS, and it is the home of the Large Hadron Collider.
The site near the Chooz nuclear power station in northern France where the Double Chooz experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from the reactors.

facility:cjpl.name: China Jinping Underground Laboratory
facility:cjpl.operator_text: Tsinghua University, together with Yalong River Hydropower Development Company

summary.plain: The world's deepest underground physics laboratory, built beside a hydropower tunnel under the Jinping mountains in southwest China. Over two kilometres of rock overhead make it an extremely quiet place to search for dark matter.
The southern-hemisphere site of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, in the Atacama Desert of Chile near ESO's Paranal Observatory.

facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.name: Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Laboratory
facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:daya-bay-reactor-neutrino-lab.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A set of underground experimental halls near the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power plants in Guangdong, China, built to catch antineutrinos streaming out of the reactors.

facility:desy.name: Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron
facility:desy.operator_text: A publicly funded German national research centre, member of the Helmholtz Association, financed 90% by the German Federal Ministry of Research and 10% by the City of Hamburg and the Federal State of Brandenburg

summary.plain: Germany's national laboratory for particle and accelerator physics, in Hamburg. Its HERA ring was the world's only electron-proton collider, and DESY continues to build and run major accelerator-based research facilities.

facility:fermilab.name: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory
facility:fermilab.operator_text: Fermi Research Alliance, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The United States national laboratory for particle physics, near Chicago. It builds and runs the chain of machines that produce the most intense beams of neutrinos in the world, and it hosts the DUNE experiment.
A mountain observatory in southern Arizona, home to the VERITAS gamma-ray telescopes among other instruments.
A remote farm in the Namibian highlands, about two hours from Windhoek, that hosts the H.E.S.S. gamma-ray telescopes.

facility:ill-grenoble.name: Institut Laue-Langevin
facility:ill-grenoble.operator: Institut Laue-Langevin (a tripartite French-German-British research organisation)
facility:ill-grenoble.operator_text: Institut Laue-Langevin (a tripartite French-German-British research organisation)

summary.plain: A major research reactor in Grenoble, France, mainly used to make beams of neutrons for science, and also home to the Ricochet reactor-neutrino experiment.

facility:isis-neutron-source.name: ISIS Neutron and Muon Source
facility:isis-neutron-source.operator: Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), part of UK Research and Innovation
facility:isis-neutron-source.operator_text: Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), part of UK Research and Innovation

summary.plain: A pulsed particle accelerator facility in Oxfordshire, England, that fires protons at a heavy-metal target to make neutrons and muons for materials research. In the 1990s its proton beam stop also served as a source of neutrinos for the KARMEN experiment.

facility:j-parc.name: J-PARC (Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex)
facility:j-parc.operator: Operated jointly by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)
facility:j-parc.operator_text: Operated jointly by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)

summary.plain: A large proton accelerator laboratory on the Pacific coast of Japan, run jointly by two national research organisations. Its most powerful machine drives a beam of neutrinos across the country to detectors in the mountains of western Japan.

facility:jefferson-lab.name: Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility
facility:jefferson-lab.operator_text: SURATech, LLC (a partnership of the Southeastern Universities Research Association and Virginia Tech, with four subcontractors) for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The U.S. national laboratory for nuclear physics in Newport News, Virginia. Its CEBAF accelerator fires a continuous beam of electrons at atomic nuclei to study the quarks and gluons that make up protons and neutrons.

facility:juno-jiangmen.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:juno-jiangmen.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A giant underground hall in southern China, dug into a hill near Jiangmen, that holds the JUNO neutrino detector deep beneath the rock so cosmic rays cannot swamp its measurements.

facility:kamioka-observatory.name: Kamioka Observatory (ICRR, University of Tokyo)
facility:kamioka-observatory.operator: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo
facility:kamioka-observatory.operator_text: Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a mine in the Japanese Alps, a kilometre beneath a mountain. The rock above screens out most cosmic rays, so very rare signals from neutrinos can be seen.

intervals.label: National Laboratory for High Energy Physics

facility:kek.name: KEK (High Energy Accelerator Research Organization)
facility:kek.operator: Inter-University Research Institute Corporation High Energy Accelerator Research Organization
facility:kek.operator_text: Inter-University Research Institute Corporation High Energy Accelerator Research Organization

summary.plain: Japan's national accelerator laboratory at Tsukuba, founded in 1971. Its 12 GeV proton accelerator made the first long-distance beam of neutrinos ever aimed at a detector hundreds of kilometres away.

facility:kit-karlsruhe.name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Campus North

summary.plain: A large German research campus north of Karlsruhe that hosts the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe, home to the KATRIN neutrino-mass experiment.

A research infrastructure of two neutrino detectors built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea: ARCA off the coast of Sicily, Italy, and ORCA off Toulon, France. Strings of light sensors watch for faint flashes made by neutrinos from space and from the Earth's atmosphere.
A Swiss nuclear power plant on the Rhine that has hosted the CONUS+ reactor-neutrino experiment since late 2023.

aliases: Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory site
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.name: LHAASO (Daocheng)
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.operator: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
facility:lhaaso-daocheng.operator_text: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A high-altitude observatory on Haizi Mountain in Sichuan, China, that catches cosmic rays and the highest-energy gamma rays yet seen, using several kinds of ground detectors at once.

The largest underground research laboratory in the world, built beside a motorway tunnel under the Gran Sasso mountain in central Italy. About 1400 metres of rock overhead cut the shower of cosmic particles by a factor of a million, which lets very quiet experiments run there.

facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory.name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory.operator_text: Triad National Security, LLC for the U.S. Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA)

summary.plain: A United States national laboratory in the mountains of New Mexico, founded during the Manhattan Project. Its LANSCE accelerator produces intense beams of protons and neutrons used for nuclear and particle physics, including past neutrino experiments.
The NASA balloon-launch site near McMurdo Station, Antarctica, where the ANITA neutrino instrument was launched on each of its long, high-altitude balloon flights.

MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) is a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its physics department built ABRACADABRA, a small experiment that searched for the axion, a hypothetical dark-matter particle.

facility:modane-underground-laboratory.name: Laboratoire Souterrain de Modane
facility:modane-underground-laboratory.operator_text: CNRS/IN2P3 and Universite Grenoble-Alpes; a national IN2P3 platform attached to the Laboratoire de Physique Subatomique et Cosmologie (LPSC) in Grenoble since 2019

summary.plain: An underground physics laboratory built into the middle of a road tunnel through the French Alps, under 1700 metres of rock. It is the deepest underground laboratory in Europe and hosts sensitive searches for dark matter and rare nuclear decays.

facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory
facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory.operator_text: UT-Battelle, LLC (a partnership of the University of Tennessee and Battelle Memorial Institute) for the U.S. Department of Energy

summary.plain: The United States' largest multiprogram science laboratory, in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. It runs the Spallation Neutron Source, whose intense proton beam also produces one of the world's best sources of neutrinos for the COHERENT experiment.

A giant outdoor laboratory in the Argentine pampas that catches ultra-high-energy cosmic rays: tanks of water spread over an area the size of Rhode Island, watched by telescopes that see the faint light of particle showers in the night sky.
